#1955. Celtic AGM latest as O'Neill talks long-term future and tense CSC visit

For Martin O'Neill, it has already been a hectic week. On Monday evening, he attended a meeting at Greenock Celtic Supporters' Club alongside interim chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, and chief financial officer Chris McKay. Over 120 fans were present as the Celtic manager and board faced, according to the club, 'hard but fair' questioning.

Less than 24 hours later, O'Neill found himself in Dingwall with assistant coaches Mark Fotheringham and Stephen McManus watching Celtic B lose 2-0 to Ross County in the Scottish Challenge Cup.

That's all before two crucial home fixtures against Besiktas in the Europa League and Kilmarnock in the William Hill Premiership come into the fray.

The 74-year-old sat down ahead of the tie with Besiktas to discuss Monday's meeting, his long-term future, and the club's upcoming Annual General Meeting (AGM).

"First of all, I wasn't really aware of the meeting, so it was kind of an ad hoc thing," O'Neill explained. "But I obviously was around. I spoke to Michael [Nicholson] and he said that they were going to meet.

"And I said, well, I wouldn't mind going down to it if that was the case, obviously to experience what the fans would be asking.

"The meeting itself was, I think you could use the word robust, yes, firm, but very orderly questioning.

"And trying to give the answers that, not necessarily what people are looking for, because I'm not so sure that will ever reach a satisfactory stage for a while anyway. But, yeah, it was really interesting and an experience.

"I probably didn't really need to go to a meeting, but these people were big Celtic fans. And naturally, I think both board and supporters, I thought there was a wanting the best for the football club.

"At the end of the day, there are bad times and I think that you should face up to that. Was everything answered by the board and myself to their satisfaction? One, you'd have to ask the people there at the time what was there.

"There was no shouting. It wasn't like the AGM that appeared [last year]. The shouting had taken place before the meeting."

Indeed, as O'Neill and company arrived in Greenock, a number of Celtic supporters wearing balaclavas were outside the supporters' club, voicing their own concerns.

"To me, I think that was the saddest thing," O'Neill continued. "Would I have ever, in any day, ever thought that Celtic fans would be clothed in balaclavas before a meeting? Even if they were disapproving of what was happening. I think that's really disappointing.

"I do find it hard to get my head round that kind of stuff.

"I think if you've got a dispute or something, I think you should be brave enough to show your face doing it.

"[It was] just on the way in. I don't know whether they expected me to be there or not, but it doesn't really matter. It was just regardless of who was there."

The hope is that this year's AGM doesn't entail similar hostilities. The last iteration was adjourned early following animosity between the hierarchy and supporters.

It's understood the 2026 AGM will take place in early December in person.

"I would expect to be at it as a manager," O'Neill said. "So if given an opportunity to answer some of the things and if they want to hear from the manager, I would have no problem.

"I hope it's similar to what Monday night was in terms of the questions and fairness and not falling into what it was last year."

As O'Neill discusses myriad off-pitch matters, it's easy to forget he's Celtic's football manager.

"People are asking me now if it’s something I’m going to continue to do," he added. "No, my main job depends on results and winning some football matches. That’s the most important thing."

Contracted at Celtic Park until the end of this season, O'Neill's deal has the option of a further 12 months.

This time last year, he was two games into what was meant to be the most fleeting of interim spells.

Wilfried Nancy's disastrous reign came and went and O'Neill returned in January, winning the double and staying on as permanent manager in the summer.

When asked if this was his final season in charge, O'Neill responded: "I can’t imagine anybody asking me back. Seriously, I can’t imagine that happening.

"Listen, I didn’t come in here today to give a final word at this minute."

If the coming months are to be his last, how important is it to go out on a high?

"It would be nice to see the club that I knew intimately from 2000 – having followed from a distance since my school days – be successful.

"Did I ever think I’d see a day when 75,000 people would descend on a UEFA Cup final day, with no arrests? There are still pictures on the wall here and all you see is a sea of green and white. To see that again, that would be your dream."

Celtic, though, could not be further away from reaching another European final. Sunday's defeat to Falkirk was their sixth in 10 matches, with Besiktas up next in the Europa League.

From their first three fixtures in the competition, Celtic are pointless, heightening criticism on O'Neill and his coaches.

"Everyone is a tactician now, that’s the whole point," he said. "Everybody is a football manager. There are people who have got jobs in football now – at football clubs – because they played PlayStation Manager.

"Honestly, it’s extraordinary. But it does not bother me, honestly, it doesn’t. People talk about tactics but in my semi-defence, no-one talked about tactics when we won the seven games to win the league [last season]. Or the 14 games we won before we got beat.

"And you know what, you’re right to think – if you got beaten in a game – that maybe somebody has out-thought you. Absolutely. You’re right to think that.

"[Falkirk manager] John McGlynn has every right to be proud of his side after beating us and to have had the upper hand."

Despite recent form, O'Neill remains more determined than ever to turn things around.

"I'm supposed to be the driver of the club," he quipped.

That said, the 74-year-old is well aware of the threat Besiktas, who sit eighth in the 36-team Europa League table, pose.

"I think these games are really hard for us," O'Neill said. "I think there are teams in the Europa League who are capable of playing in the Champions League and getting results in the Champions League at this minute. However, we're in the Europa League.

"We haven't got a point on the board. We're going to try and do something about it if we can on Thursday and then ask the question.

"But I think that no-one has ever lost the first three and qualified for the competition. So, we’ll be up against it. We're definitely up against it. But are we capable? Yeah, I have to believe that."

"But I think there are mitigating circumstances involved. So it's not us accepting it. Hopefully, they watched the same first half as what the staff did.

"It was a good game in the first half. It was a proper local derby. And then it's just circumstances that killed it.

"There are individual errors. But there are certain things that we shouldn't be doing - like taking a short corner in the first place.

#1952. Hearts accounts reveal £2.4m loss and transfer spend amid bad news on Calvin Miller injury

Hearts have announced a loss of £2.4million after investing heavily to return to European football this season.

The Tynecastle club backed Derek McInnes after he took over as boss in the summer of 2025. The Jambos’ thrilling Scottish Premiership title challenge went to the last day of the season when they lost to Celtic at Parkhead to finish second to the Hoops.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hearts lost to Sturm Graz in the Champions League qualifiers and then to Benfica in the Europa League, but victory over Rapid Vienna saw Wouter Vrancken’s side make it to the league phase of the Conference League, where they face Swiss side Thun on Thursday.

Hearts also reported a turnover of £23.1m for the 2025/26 financial year, are also in “positive” discussions about further investment to help Vrancken in the January transfer window and are confident of a “significantly improved financial result” in a year’s time.

The club’s financial results also revealed that staff costs went up eight per cent “with player acquisition costs of £7.8m across the year, reflecting significant investment in the playing squad”.

A statement on Hearts’ official website said: “The club took a deliberate decision to invest in the playing squad from a position of financial strength, helping secure a return to European league phase football for 2026/27. This additional investment in squad wages, combined with the absence of European income, resulted in an operating loss of £2.4m for the year.

“With European income returning and further progress in player trading, the club anticipates a significantly improved financial result in 2026/27.

“Strong underlying revenue growth offset much of the loss of European income for the 2025/26 financial year, with sponsorship and advertising income up 37 per cent and retail and hospitality income up 17 per cent, reflecting continued commercial progress and support from partners and fans alike.

“The club continued to benefit from exceptional financial backing from its benefactors and Foundation of Hearts members, and extends its sincere thanks for their continued commitment and support.

“The increased investment in the playing squad and football operations was supported by an investment from Tony Bloom towards the end of the previous financial year, which strengthened the club’s financial position and provided capacity to invest in improving the playing squad.

“As an equity investment, this funding is reflected in the balance sheet rather than recognised as income in the profit and loss account.

“The reported operating loss of £2.4m includes £1.8m of gains from player trading and is stated before depreciation, amortisation and finance costs. Further gains will be reflected in the 2026/27 financial year following player trading activity completed in July and August 2026.

“The club is also engaged in positive discussions regarding further investment to support the continued, measured pursuit of the club’s ambitions. The club’s balance sheet remains robust, with the accounts reporting net assets of £20.3m at the June 30 2026 financial year-end.”

Meanwhile, Vrancken revealed Calvin Miller will require surgery on a knee injury that will keep him out for two months.

Both Tomas Magnusson and Miller came off during the first half of the Jambos’ 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final defeat to Edinburgh rivals Hibs at Hampden on Sunday. The Iceland midfielder was taken to hospital with concussion and the former Celtic, Morton and Falkirk attacker left the national stadium on crutches and his knee in a brace.

Vrancken, who will be without 10 first-team players for the game against FC Thun, was asked about Miller and said: “It will be two months, let’s say, depending on what the surgery says because it’s a meniscus injury. It’s a pity, but it is what it is.

“Tomas is doing good. The day after was already a lot better. There is a protocol, of course, with concussions. He will be for sure back after the (international) break.”

#1950. Celtic unwanted 'world record' quip, best starting XI admission and player who might cry if he scores

Celtic host Besiktas on Guy Fawkes Night hoping to rediscover the fireworks of exactly two years ago when a Champions League masterclass inflicted a 3-1 defeat on RB Leipzig.

The decline of the Parkhead club in Europe since that run to the knockout stages that saw them come within seconds of taking Bayern Munich to extra-time for a place in the last 16 has been well documented.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It should also be noted that such success on the continent is the exception as Celtic's two previous November 5 results in Europe will testify, namely a 4-1 home defeat by Sparta Prague in 2020 and a 2-1 home loss to Molde in 2015.

As bonfires are lit across the country, Celtic's focus will be on preventing their Europa League flame from burning out as they go in search of their first points of the campaign after successive defeats by Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

One of only four teams still on zero points after three matches, Martin O'Neill's side are only being kept off the bottom of the 36-team table due to the fact that minnows Ararat Armenia have a worse goal difference.

There are still 15 points left to play for so all is not lost, but the recovery needs to start now.

“I was told that any team who’s lost their first three games haven’t made it through, so it doesn’t augur brilliantly for us if that’s the case,” O’Neill said during his pre-match press conference on Wednesday.

“So if we go on for a fourth one, then that would be a world record.

“We’re definitely running out of matches, no question about it. But we are capable of still qualifying if, let’s say, 10 points is the mark.

”It means you really have to go away and win, not draw."

There are six survivors from the Celtic team that played in that statement win over Leipzig. Alistair Johnston, Cameron Carter-Vickers, Auston Trusty and Callum McGregor started while Liam Scales and Hyun-Jun Yang appeared off the bench.

Johnston and Yang are both unavailable although the latter has returned to training and could return as soon as Sunday, when the Scottish champions host Kilmarnock in the Premiership.

After their weekend 2-0 defeat at Falkirk, Celtic have won just three of their last 10 matches in all competitions and O'Neill admits he is still unsure of his best starting XI.

"I keep getting asked this question and until I know exactly what everyone can do at the football club, then I probably won't know that," he said. "It's not always knowing about your best team because we've had a lot of games and we're rotating a bit as well to try and save some legs, save a little bit of energy.

"I think it's our ninth game in about 20 odd days. We're in these competitions and we're trying to do our best.

"Once each player has had an opportunity, for instance [Jordan] Latomba hasn't really had a proper opportunity, and once players get a couple of matches then you can make a decision. But your best team might be for a certain game and your best team for European competition might be something else."

Former Celtic striker Oh Hyeon-gyu returns to Parkhead for the first time since his 2024 summer departure. The South Korea international netted 12 goals in 18 months in Glasgow but only started six of his 47 appearances.

After being signed under Ange Postecoglou, he found game time increasingly hard to come by under Brendan Rodgers. But a move to Genk in the summer of 2024 allowed him to move his career forward and he joined Besiktas in January for a fee of around £12million.

Speaking in English at a pre-match media conference, Oh said: “I’m so excited. It’s very special for me to be back here.

“I couldn’t speak English properly back then but everyone welcomed me like family here. And Celtic became like my second home. Maybe I will be emotional if I score but I will give everything for Besiktas.”

Reflecting on his time in Scotland, Oh added: “I came here as a young boy with a dream. It was sometimes hard for me, sometimes good for me.

“I have got good memories here. I always be grateful for everything and the fans. If I score, maybe I will cry. I learned a lot about my position from Kyogo Furuhashi and Adam Idah.

“In my last season here, I didn’t play for the last six months so it was a hard time for me. But I’m very happy to be back here because I love Celtic so much. It has a special place in my heart.

“After I left Celtic, it was good motivation for me. I wanted to show what I could do and how much I have improved. Finally I am back here and I have to show them.”

That was back on August 7 in the EFL's curtain raiser to the season, when the Red Dragons visited the Riverside Stadium for a first-round Carabao Cup fixture.

Just after the hour mark, Lankshear settled the issue on his debut with a technically exquisite hooked volley. A televised audience and not just those present on Teesside watched on in admiration.

'Middlesbrough get their first glimpse of a striker who could be a hero in waiting' were the prescient words by the Sky Sports commentator.

Just under three months on, the 21-year-old remains the talk of the Championship in many respects ahead of Boro's first league meeting with Wrexham in 2026-27.

Lankshear has scored 15 times in 16 appearances for Boro in league and cup. The former Tottenham Hotspur frontman, who had a spell earlier in his career at Sheffield United, has scored in his last five successive fixtures since the last international break - netting on seven occasions.

His 13 Championship goals have arrived in 13 league appearances, the best record for any Boro player at the start of a season since the legendary George Camsell in 1926.

Speak to the forward, who arrived for an initial £10m in the summer—and he will be quick to remind people that his tally so far this term is 16 and not 15. Lankshear also scored for England under-21s in their September fixture against Kazakhstan.

His feats have even led to some talk about a possible maiden senior call-up. That is surely one for the future as opposed to the present, but the fact that it is being talked about is significant.

Sensibly, Boro chief Kim Hellberg is circumspect regarding such conjecture and rightly so.

Last season, there was plenty of gushing talk about the prowess of the player wearing the number seven shirt currently worn by Lankshear in Hayden Hackney. His season would ultimately end in tears of frustration.

Asked about the prospect of a full call-up, Hellberg, very much wearing his manager’s hat - his high-fliers are seeking to extend their unbeaten league sequence to 12 games this evening - said: "No, it would be better if he was playing with us and training with us, to be very frank. I'm going to be honest…

"So, that's my answer. Then, of course, for him, everyone wants to play for the country and everyone is happy with that.

"We take a lot of pride in our football club if they are involved in the under-21s or the senior team or whatever it is for their country, and we know that's a big thing for the players and they work very hard every day to be there.

"I think that's also one thing that's been seen, that we have more call-ups this year than last year, because we are in a good position and we have a lot of good players. We will see and that's the same thing with all the players."

One player who is likely to be on international duty next month is key Australian midfielder Riley McGree.

It had been expected that the creative force would also be on Socceroos business at the Asian Cup, which was scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia in January and early February. But it has been postponed because of a series of terrorist attacks on the host country and has been rescheduled for December 2027.

Amid a key period, McGree's availability would be welcome from a Boro perspective. The 28-year-old has already started over half of the league games that he managed in 2025-26.

On McGree, who has started 10 of Boro's 13 league games thus far, Hellberg commented: "I think Riley is an absolutely perfect player for us in how he plays.

"He has so much quality in finding spaces to connect with other players and he's involved in a lot of good things. Often when you watch the game after, you see so many good movements that are off the ball, where he opens up space for people and understands the game in a brilliant way.

"I'm very happy with the amount of game time he has been having on a high level. You still need to manage and balance things, but that goes for everyone.

"But I think he's taken big steps to play even more and it's a case of of just keep going, improving and working hard with that. Everyone wants him on the pitch as much as possible."

McGree and Boro are in a good place. That extends to off the pitch with head of football Kieran Scott and recruitment supremo Chris Jones signing new long-term deals this week. Paul Watson has arrived from Brentford as chief technical officer.

Hellberg added: "They have done a brilliant job. We talked about signing players and getting them here. The recruitment, how we work with players and all those things is a key thing."

The goal cancelled out Jan Bednarek's opener for Porto but the hosts went back in front through Gabri Veiga in the 71st minute before Jakob Kiwior made it 3-1 with 10 minutes remaining.

Napoli were then reduced to 10 men in the 88th minute when Rafa Marín was shown a red card for denying a goalscoring opportunity, with Samu Aghehowa converting the resultant penalty.

Billy Gilmour completed the full 90 minutes for Napoli - the first time the Scotland midfielder has started and finished a match for the Italian club since September.

McTominay, meanwhile, has now scored three goals in his last two Champions League appearances after netting a brace in a 4-3 win over Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona last month. He followed that with another double in a 3-3 draw with Roma in Serie A.

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli will hope the talismanic midfielder can bring his goalscoring form to the international scene ahead of the upcoming Nations League matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

McTominay missed the Belgian's maiden camp last month due to the minimally invasive medical procedure which also saw him sit out four Napoli matches.

His goal against Porto takes McTominay's overall Champions League tally to eight, making him Scotland's leading scorer in the competition since it rebranded from the European Cup in 1993, three ahead of Kenny Miller and Ian Durrant on five.

Napoli host Lazio on Sunday in their final Serie A match before the international break, with McTominay and Gilmour due to meet with up the Scotland squad the following day.

#1946. Sheffield Wednesday manager Dave Challinor clear what his style challenge entails

When it came to his new players, the Chester-born manager's first priority was clarity – a word that regularly cropped up in his first press conference. When it comes to the supporters, it is about delivering attractive football – and he is clear what that means to him.

As Henrik Pedersen discovered to his cost, winning alone is not enough at League One Wednesday.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dane only needed two defeats on the back of a nine-match unbeaten run to be shown the door at Hillsborough. But it was about more than that – his football just was not doing it for the supporters.

So Challinor knows he has to play with panache. Fortunately, he does not think he will have to change much to produce it with the squad he has been furnished with.

The problem is, one man's entertainment is another man's boring football. Some love pure passing, others are bored by tippy-tappy – "Gerri’ forward" is not an unusual thing to hear on a Yorkshire terrace.

"If you look at the last few years I would suggest some of the teams that have played the most attractive football have got promoted in Birmingham and Cardiff," argues a manager who led Stockport County before resigning when the Hatters lost the League One play-off final to Bolton Wanderers in May.

"Attractive football is different for everybody.

"How Brighton go about it in the Premier League is very different to how Arsenal go about it.

"The Arsenal fans will tell you that the football they play is really attractive because they won the Premier League last year.

"What this football club needs and wants is different from 20 miles away maybe."

It begged the question: what is his definition of attractive football?

"I want us to be possession-based but purposeful in that," he says. "I want us to play forward and be aggressive with and without the ball and play with good ball speed.

"I want to make the team we play against defend from their box."

It feels like everyone is starting from a position of clarity.

Challinor worked with sporting director Simon Wilson for five years at Stockport, and although he was careful to take a while choosing Pedersen's replacement, and to remove himself from certain discussions so there we no accusations of bias, it was clear he wanted what the 51-year-old provides.

And Challinor knows what he is walking into.

"Carlton Palmer was the manager at Stockport when I went there," he says. "I grew up as a Liverpool fan and go back to the early 90s when Sheffield Wednesday as a football club were in the Premier League and FA Cup finals. The history is there.

"You don't need to be told if you're involved in football around what Sheffield Wednesday is. I shared a car with Brian Barry Murphy for six years at Bury.

"I know Steve Haslam really well. I played with Steve at Bury and he played for me at Fylde.

"But I think everyone involved in football understands the magnitude and size of this football club."

He took time to reflect whilst out of work.

"My wife works from home and didn't like me in the house very often," he smiles. "When you come out, there's probably only so much you can do.

"You go on a few holidays, you go to other clubs. I've made some brilliant trips over the summer to go and see some brilliant people.

"I went up to Celtic and spoke to Martin O'Neill, who was amazing. I watched them training and Martin said I wouldn't learn anything from that.

"But just to watch him and how he works as he's someone I've got a massive amount of respect for was great.

"H's don a not too dissimilar journey to him in terms of starting in non-league so you take an awful lot from those things."

He comes promising evolution, not revolution.

"I just spoke to the players at the first meeting," says Challinor. "The big thing for me will be clarity around what our structure will be, roles and responsibilities, standards, behaviours that we need to live every day.

"They'll get honesty, I expect them to be honest with us.

"I won't ask them to do something that I can't do, except maybe run around on a football pitch now.

"It'll be a steady process, but I think you'll see some things that are different.

"Structurally, there'll be some little bits, clarity and simplicity around what we want to do in certain areas of the pitch.

"We need to get some excitement into especially this place. That comes from being positive, playing forward, being purposeful with our possession, making the other team defend for long periods, and getting the supporters off their seats."

Bruce's side have not win a competitive game since September 19. They visit Bromley in the FA Cup this weekend and are 22nd in League Two.

Asked whether his job is in jeopardy, Bruce said: "It's not about me. If there's a fight to be had, I'll have it, but I know the buck stops with me."

On his side's winless streak extending, he continued: "In large parts of it, there wasn't really that much in the game.

"They counter-attacked us in the first half and scored. We didn't do enough to win the game. I think we huffed and puffed.

"As I've just said to the players in the dressing room, to win football matches, you have to show a little bit more than that. If we are going to get out of the trouble that we're in, we need to start showing a bit more than we did."

Despite being available for the competition, Jili Buyabu - dismissed for elbowing a Swindon Town player in last Saturday's League Two fixture - was not involved, with Bruce revealing he had been ordered to stay away from the training ground following his senseless dismissal.

Bruce continued: "I've not seen him since the Swindon game.

"It doesn't take a rocket scientist to realise why he's not been involved.

"I accept people make mistakes, I don't accept certain other things. When he comes back into the group, he needs to show an appetite to wear the shirt in the right way. On Saturday, he didn't do that."

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A defining performance of the Ruben Amorim era so far, everyone played their role stupendously – and that includes the Portuguese, who tactically outclassed his counterpart. As a result, the scores from us were rather high in our post-match ratings.

Looking at the ratings from elsewhere, Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) gave the performance an eight, also giving Amorim that score, too.

In terms of the players’ performances, Goncalo Ramos was the lowest, with a still passable score of a 6. However, Ardon Jashari and Davide Bartesaghi were also given these scores, understandable after coming off the bench.

With 6.5s, Koni De Winter, Yunus Musah and Alphadjo Cisse were all very solid, with the latter almost grabbing a fourth in the game. Mario Gila, Strahinja Pavlovic and Sankhoun Diawara were given 7s, as did Luka Modric and the first goalscorer Christian Pulisic.

The Diavolo’s French duo – Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot – were awarded a score of 7.5, whilst Diego Moreira was given an eight for his goal and two assists.

Moving to Corriere dello Sport, Amorim was given an eight again. Ramos scored the lowest again, at a six, whilst Musah, Diawara, Pavlovic and De Winter were given 6.5. Gila, Modric, Pulisic and Rabiot were given 7s. Then, Maignan was given a 7.5, Moreira, again, was given an 8/10.

Finally, Tuttosport’s ratings were largely the same. Ramos was given a downgrade to a 5/10, whilst Moreira was given another eight. The French goalkeeper kept his second-best position with a 7.5 – alongside Rabiot – thanks to his big saves, whilst Diawara was also given a bump up to a 7, thanks to an impressive derby debut.

Elsewhere, Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Musah and Pulisic were given 6.5s, Modric played a 7/10 game and Amorim was given a 7.5.

#1942. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: ‘We have no fear at all’, Pau Torres identifies Barca weakness

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 06:55, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 07:08

Barcelona have been through a run of tricky games, losing their 100% record in the Champions League and La Liga to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, and now, after recovering with two wins, they face another big challenge. On Tuesday, Barcelona host Aston Villa at the Camp Nou.

The English side have won every game in the European competition and are unbeaten in five Premier League matches. That is why Pau Torres, an undisputed starter for Aston Villa, is not afraid at all of the game against Barcelona.

‘We have no fear at all, but we do have respect. We know how difficult it will be, but nothing is impossible. We will try to compete with our own weapons’ - he said in an interview with Catalan newspaper Sport.

The 29-year-old defender also pointed out what to exploit in the contest.

Barcelona, under the management of Hansi Flick, are characterised by heavy pressing in the attacking half, which forces a high defensive line to keep up with the rest of the team. That space is something for Aston Villa to exploit, as Pau Torres explained, based on the profile of their trio of very quick attackers, including a Brazilian.

‘This year we have very vertical players, such as Ibrahim Mbaye, Alysson and Nicolas Jackson himself. They work very well when opponents leave space behind the defence.’

Of course, there is a way to attack, but for more than 60% of the time Barcelona’s opponents will be defending. Focus is a must if they are to avoid conceding against Barcelona, who have scored 57 times in 14 matches this season. ‘If we want to get a positive result, we will have to be alert defensively.’

Pau Torres also has a special mission. As a left-sided centre-back, he could come up against right winger Lamine Yamal several times because of the cover he will have to provide for left-back Ian Maatsen, who is known for being very attacking.

‘When you play this type of match, you always want to face the best to find out what level you are at. It will be a pleasure to play against Lamine and have to mark him on some occasions.

He always surprises, he is unpredictable and, often, just one player to mark him is not enough. We will have to be very alert to the cover from team-mates.’

The clash, which promises to be an interesting one, kicks off at 8pm UK time on Tuesday. Aston Villa share top spot in the Champions League league phase with Paris Saint-Germain, who are ahead on goals scored, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis. Barcelona are looking to recover after losing 4-2 to leaders Paris Saint-Germain in the last round.

Rasmus Kristensen has revealed he was “completely broken” after his maiden campaign on Leeds United’s books.

The 29-year-old arrived at Elland Road in the summer of 2022, making a move from Red Bull Salzburg for a fee in the region of £10m.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He was recruited to be Luke Ayling’s successor at right-back but the Denmark international struggled for consistency in West Yorkshire.

Leeds were relegated at the end his debut campaign and he spent the following two seasons out on loan before departing permanently.

In an interview with Ajax Life, the defender has opened up on the difficulties he endured at Elland Road.

He said: “I suffered from stress and depression. After that season, I was completely broken. I always saw myself only as a footballer.

“When I walked through the city or sat in a restaurant, I worried about training or the next match. If you do that, you become mentally exhausted.”

Kristensen spent the 2023/24 season on loan at Roma before linking up with Eintracht Frankfurt for the 2024/25 campaign.

The latter signed him on a permanent basis in 2025 but he is now back in his native Denmark with FC Midtjylland.

Reflecting on his first temporary stint away from Leeds, Kristensen said: “Rome was beautiful, but as a footballer, I found no joy there. Wherever I played, I felt pressure. Football is a religion in Italy - even more so than in Leeds and Amsterdam.”

Kristensen now appears to be in a better place, enjoying his football in his homeland. He will face his former club Ajax tomorrow (November 5), when Midtjylland host the Dutch giants in the Europa Conference League.

He said: “Before, after a bad training session, I would think ‘f**k football’. Now, I can put things into perspective more easily when I get home. As a father, I enjoy the game more.

“My wife and I enjoyed having our family and friends close by again.”

#1939. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1938. Middlesbrough FC and Sheffield United's rivals West Ham United confirm Scott Parker appointment

Sheffield United and Middlesbrough’s Championship rivals West Ham United have appointed Scott Parker as their new head coach.

Nuno Espirito Santo was relieved of his duties yesterday (November 3) with the Hammers sat eighth in the Championship table.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

West Ham have wasted little time replacing him, turning to former Hammers and England midfielder Parker.

The 46-year-old was most recently employed by Burnley and has also managed Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Club Brugge. He is something of a Championship promotion specialist having led all of his English employers into the Premier League.

After taking the reins at the London Stadium, Parker said: “It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a club that means so much to me and my family. A lot of very fond memories of my time here - four years of probably the best football I played in my career.

“There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn’t have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly.

“More than anything, this is an opportunity that I am very excited about. I feel privileged and honoured to be the guy that wants to lead us back to the Premier League and be the head coach of this football club at this moment in time.

“My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion - it’s absolutely running through and that's the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible. That's exactly why I'm here and why I want to be here.

“From my first calls with Karim [Virani] and Daniel [Křetínský], it was clear they have a shared vision and desire to return the club to the Premier League as quickly as possible. I share that ambition and I’m very confident we can achieve it.

“I’ve been in this division three times and I've got out of this division three times. This is a tough division, there is absolutely no denying it. And I will use every ounce of my experience, every ounce of my knowledge, to have an understanding of what we're going to need to bring consistency.

“And that's going to be the key word for all of us really. The consistency of what we do and the commitment levels that we go to will give us the best opportunity to get out of this division and be the team that we can be.”

West Ham sit level on points with ninth-placed Sheffield United and six points adrift of table-toppers Middlesbrough.

#1936. Man Utd next manager: Unai Emery to Old Trafford latest as fresh update emerges on Carrick replacement

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 07:07

Manchester United continue to admire Aston Villa manager Unai Emery as they consider potential alternatives should Michael Carrick leave Old Trafford.

However, convincing the Spaniard to abandon his successful project at Villa Park could prove extremely difficult, with questions over how much authority he would receive in Manchester.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are also emerging as leading contenders, potentially giving the Red Devils several alternative options in their managerial search.

According to TEAMtalk, United decision-makers still highly regard Emery, and the club continues to explore potential replacements for Carrick behind the scenes.

The Spaniard has transformed Aston Villa into top-four contenders and guided them to Europa League success, establishing significant influence over the club's footballing operations.

That control has been central to his achievements, and Villa would be expected to fight hard to retain their manager if United formalised their interest.

Although the opportunity to take charge of one of Europe's biggest clubs could appeal to Emery, sources believe the level of authority available at Old Trafford would be a major stumbling block.

At Villa, Emery has been allowed considerable freedom over his methods and decision-making. United's structure and expectations are different, potentially making the role less attractive than it initially appears.

United are understood to be preparing for different scenarios despite publicly backing Carrick, with Emery remaining among the names held in high regard internally.

Former Newcastle United boss Howe is also heavily linked, with director of football Jason Wilcox reportedly favouring him. Meanwhile, director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is believed to prefer Nagelsmann.

Emery would be an impressive appointment on paper, but United may be wasting valuable time pursuing a manager who has little obvious reason to leave Villa.

He has built a successful project at Villa Park, enjoys considerable control and has established the club as a regular competitor for major honours.

Moving to Old Trafford would mean taking on a rebuilding job at a club that has struggled with managerial instability for more than a decade. There is no guarantee he would receive the same influence that has helped him thrive in Birmingham.

United should therefore concentrate on more realistic alternatives, with Howe potentially offering an attractive option given his Premier League experience and previous success at Newcastle.

Nagelsmann also deserves serious consideration, particularly if Vivell can convince the club's hierarchy that he is the right long-term appointment.

Emery's reputation makes him an understandable target, but United need a manager who genuinely wants the job and can work within their structure. On the available evidence, Howe and Nagelsmann may be more realistic options.

#1934. Classy hat trick secures victory!

A magnificent second half hat-trick from midfielder Keith Chamberlain meant that a dominant performance was reflected in the scoreline as National Over 60s Football Champions, East Sussex, cruised to a comfortable 6-1 victory against group rivals Kent, in the warm sunshine at Bexhill College last Sunday.

A spectacular, unstoppable volley from the left-hand corner of the penalty box arrowed into the bottom right hand corner earning Chamberlain his first.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

His second, another volley; was calmly placed beyond the reach of the visitor’s keeper from closer range.

Chamberlain finished his hat trick with East Sussex’s sixth and final goal of the game.

This time, his beautifully placed curling effort from 20 yards into the same right-hand corner, left the opposition keeper and defenders watching on motionless.

Although the men in orange and black were dominant by every measure and played attractive football throughout the game, Kent had their moments and only a stunning double save from East Sussex keeper Koosha Movevagh prevented the visitors from scoring in the first half.

Player Manager Alan Osman, had earlier opened the scoring, nodding home a perfectly flighted cross from fellow front man Colin Riggs midway through the first half.

Riggs had an outstanding game. Although he didn’t find himself on the scoresheet; his selfless running and his constant willingness to receive the ball to feet and lay it on for the East Sussex midfielders and wide men were critical in securing the win.

Riggs was inches away from scoring after a superb Osman cross in the first half and he looked certain to score in the second half when a chipped pass from skipper Andy Williams put him through one on one with the Kent keeper, yet what looked like the perfect lob somehow bounced over the vacant goal.

After Osman's opener, Tim Kryezui scored his first competitive goal for the men in orange and black, when he made it 2-0, before half time.

Tim had an excellent first half in his attacking midfield role and the way he calmly rounded the keeper and finished a superb back to front team passing move, characterised his performance on the day.

Nigel Pamplin made his debut replacing Tim in the second half and ‘Pamps’ incisive link up play contributed to many attractive East Sussex attacking moves.

The East Sussex back four of Dave Pearson. Bob Smith, John O’Meara and Steve Burge were solid in defence and comfortable in possession throughout.

Ed Greenwood and Steve Turner carried real threat from wide midfield positions in the first half, whilst skipper Williams sat in his usual deep midfield anchor role.

Kent scored their consolation with ten minutes to go, shortly after Williams left the field with an injury.

East Sussex’s next game in the competition is a big one, away against main group rivals Farnham and District, on 29th November 2026.

#1931. Real Madrid: how Franco Mastantuono is faring on loan at Fiorentina

By Axel Clody | 03 Nov 2026 07:08

Franco Mastantuono has finally been getting consecutive opportunities in European football. After a first year of ups and downs at Real Madrid, the young Argentine was loaned to Fiorentina this season and has played in all of the club’s games.

The high point of his spell, which began in August, has been the hat-trick against Venezia in the fourth round of Serie A, a 4-2 comeback win that made him the youngest Argentine player to score three times in Europe’s top five leagues. The first two goals were very much in the right winger’s style: cutting inside onto his left foot and placing the finish.

That result, however, was the only time the Florence side managed to win in Serie A. Fiorentina’s campaign has produced six defeats and two draws, which is why they sit on the edge of the relegation zone.

Mastantuono has not been involved in a goal since, even though he remains the team’s main attacking protagonist. One of the reasons lies in the young player’s biggest challenge so far in Italy, which he admitted himself in an interview shortly after arriving in the country.

Responsible for a third of his team’s league goals, the 19-year-old forward carries the responsibility of being the ‘owner’ of the attacking department in the side managed by Paolo Vanoli. He is always sought out on the wing for an individual move and delivers: he is the leader in ground duels won in the whole of Serie A (48, along with two other players) and third in successful dribbles, 18, alongside Nico Paz.

‘I am always looking to attack, going at opponents and showing personality’ - he explained his profile to the newspaper Gazzetta dello Sport on 4 September.

Thanks to his ability to win individual duels, he also constantly puts himself in a position to shoot, and is third in that statistic in the league too (33, the leader in the Fiorentina squad). He also provides passes for his team-mates’ shots (17 in all, 17th in the league and top in the squad).

The Argentine generates a lot of attacking play, that is undeniable, but the finishing of moves has almost always been negative. He has attempted 33 shots but only nine have been on target. ‘I need to improve in many things, including my efficiency in front of goal,’ he admitted, also to Gazzetta.

Another feature of his game, dribbling, also has issues that hamper Fiorentina and kill the team’s attacks. Mastantuono often wins a one-on-one and, instead of passing the ball, tries another, which makes him lose it.

His success rate in dribbles and ground duels is below half of those attempted (43% and 48% respectively). Among all Serie A players, he is second for possession losses, with 20. Manager Vanoli has already identified the issue, praising the youngster as the only one capable of setting the team’s tempo.

‘He is a talent who needs to be put at the service of the team and must improve his understanding of when to dictate the team’s rhythm. He is the only one who can do that. I told him that, in Italy, we are good at noticing when a player wants to dribble. He needs to improve in one-on-one situations and understand that, if he is double-marked, there will always be a team-mate free. And that means playing as a team’ - he said on 23 October.

This, however, is still common for Franco Mastantuono’s age. It is a natural maturing process. He still looks a very promising youngster, to the same extent as when he emerged at River Plate. He does not see much fairness in the criticism he receives.

‘People demand a lot of me. I understand, I know what they expect of me. Many times they are hard on me, but I try to make the most of it. [...] I do not complain about criticism.

I am a footballer and I understand that. But people talk about things that are outside my control. I just do my job and always try to do it well’ - he told TyC Sports in early October.

Mastantuono is answering some of that criticism on the pitch and, after the frustration of missing the World Cup because of his few minutes at Real Madrid, he was part of Argentina’s latest call-up. The forward, like Nico Paz and other youngsters, will be the future of Argentina in a new era without Lionel Messi and other experienced players.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri entered last night’s game with a run of seven unbeaten and they finished the night with eight unbeaten and a fourth consecutive win. It’s a first in itself for more than 50 years, which is telling.

It’s a result which brought Gerry Cardinale to tears and it’s clear that something has really clicked at San Siro, as the player ratings showed.

Speaking at a press conference after the game, as relayed by MilanNews, the Inter coach spoke about several things, including his unfavourable record in the Derby della Madonnina.

“Compared to last year, there’s something to note about our approach to matches: the superficiality and casualness with which we handle certain situations, where we lack a bit of grit, a bit of determination, a bit of danger perception. But we need to rediscover them.

“We need to be aware that right now, despite a few more points than last year, we’ve lost something that absolutely needs to be rediscovered.”

“I couldn’t, because the forwards have had some problems in the last few days. Bonny only made himself available on the last day after two days with a fever of 39°C and severe nausea and vomiting, so we were forced to find a solution, to make a virtue of necessity, changing the system a bit.

“We knew that, in this type of match, it would be the right thing to have pace on the wings with Spence and Carlos and attack the line a bit more, as well as looking for depth in space with Diouf operating under the striker, looking for both him and Sucic between the lines.

“Unfortunately, sometimes things don’t work out, but, I repeat, we were forced to change.”

“It’s too easy to talk now that Lautaro is injured and the other two forwards aren’t feeling well. These things happen, fortunately not often. We’ll make some assessments, but we’re still happy with our four forwards, in addition to what Lavelli gives us, what Mosconi gives us, and whoever we bring in from the Under 23s.

“But, I repeat, it’s too easy to bring these things up at a time when two forwards aren’t at their best and the third is injured.”

Is there something mental that comes into play in the derby?

“There’s always something mental, I think, and history teaches us this, when you get to play another season after winning.

“So, let’s try not to throw everything away and try to rediscover some determination, some humility in doing certain things, starting with myself, because I’m primarily responsible for everything we do.

“We shouldn’t throw everything away because we’ve reached the tenth matchday and this is the first game we’ve lost. We’ve got 25 points, and last year we’d got fewer, but we’ve always been able to react, we’ve always kept our feet on the ground and our heads down to build a strong season.

“That’s what we’d like to do again this year, because we have this desire and this ambition to have another strong season; we just need to find the way to build it again.”

Nmecha said: “As soon as I entered training, I thought this level is quite similar to where I’d come from. But as soon as we entered the game, it was a completely different thing.

“I think Germany and England are very different. Even the players in terms of character, they’re a lot more, I’ll say just vicious. I like it. We’ve got good players for that as well.

“We’ve got Ethan [Ampadu], where he’s the nicest guy ever, and then on a matchday it’s like ‘what’s going on here?’.”
