Today:Everton 2 Manchester United 2Arsenal 2 Chelsea 1

Possession: Arsenal 55%-45% ChelseaShots: 16-13Shots on target: 9-5Corners: 5-3Touches in opposition box: 44-25

The final whistle is blown at the Emirates and Arsenal maintain their 100% record through three games as they have beaten Chelsea 2-1. They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

That is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

Chelsea are bringing on Welbeck for Rogers, who is jeered by the Arsenal fans. Welbeck comes on with a note, that he gives to his captain James.

Arsenal have lost a bit of their composure and structure. I suspect that’s why Arteta has turned to Mikel Merino. He screamed at his bench immediately after a messy passage of play, and Merino emerged about 20 seconds later. Merino is very much the “sensible adult” sort of player, who should calm things down. Although he hasn’t yet.

England team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a big club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

It has kicked off. Rogers is cynically tripped by Rice but the referee somehow does not see it. Rogers is incensed and marches over to Rice, who has massively got away with one there. Rice knew exactly what he was doing as he deliberately trips Rogers. That is a nasty from Rice, who avoids a booking, yet Rogers is shown a yellow card. That is frankly dreadful refereeing.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

Estevao is brought on for Chelsea in place of Neto.

Pedro wins a corner off Gabriel out on the left in front of the travelling Chelsea fans. Gusto’s delivery to the back post is caught at the second attempt by Raya.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. It is really intelligent from Havertz, who dummies it to take away Fofana and allows the ball to run through to Odegaard, who takes one touch before firing past Martinez.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Arsenal just scored the same goal they scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield. Tzolis into Odegaard, low and fast.

As it stands, Manchester City will be the only team with a 100% record after three games.

I think Chelsea are now 19 Premier League games without keeping a clean sheet, dating back to last season.

A few Chelsea players were having a moan at referee Christopher Kavanagh as they went off for half-time. But Alonso’s players need to calm down and keep their cool. There were signs the Blues’ old disciplinary problems could rear their head again with Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer being booked. Romeo Lavia also squared up to Ben White for no real reason. Chelsea have to keep 11 players on the pitch.

Possession: Arsenal 58%-42% ChelseaShots: 10-6Shots on target: 6-3Corners: 2-0Touches in opposition box: 26-13

A really enjoyable half of football, even if it was slowed down a little in the last few minutes by a series of niggly fouls. Arsenal are the better team here but Chelsea are definitely dangerous. That Neto shot off the post was evidence of how quickly they can hurt the Arsenal defence.

The first half is brought to an end and it is 1-1 going into the break at the Emirates.

Chelsea hit the post late on in the half. Chelsea counter from inside their own half and Pedro whips a ball first time down the right channel to pick out the run of Neto. The Portuguese forward drives at Gabriel inside the Arsenal box and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot. His effort comes back off the far post and Chelsea were inches away from retaking the lead.

That left side of the Arsenal defence again. Wide open for Neto to run into the space. Chelsea looking for the early ball every time.

Tensions are boiling over as Lavia and White come to blows. As Lavia shepherds the ball out of play, White threw himself to ground and wanted a free-kick. Lavia is not impressed by White’s antics and lets him know about it.

Is Palmer in some trouble? Raya catches a free-kick into his box and gets Arsenal going on the counter with a long ball forward. With Havertz getting away from him, Palmer brings him down and takes the yellow. There was another covering defender, hence why it was just a yellow.

As we approach half-time, there have been 15 shots in total from both sides in the game with nine of those being on target.

Chelsea win it just inside the Arsenal half after good defensive work from Lavia and Pedro then spots Raya off his line. The Chelsea forward therefore opts to shoot from a long way out but drags his effort wide.

White and Havertz exchange a neat one-two down Arsenal’s right, with the latter clipping the ball to the back post. Lavia, with Saka right behind him, heads away well under pressure.

That is a decent opportunity for Rogers to get his second of the game. Pedro lays it off to him on the left side of the box and Rogers tries to curl one into the far corner but it goes wide.

Tremendous game at the Emirates. Both teams attacking one another. Chelsea have a lot of space with Pedro Neto on the right and keep using that diagonal ball. Once again, though, they look suspect in defence. The Havertz equaliser could have been stopped twice, but Chelsea defence just did not react. Fofana let Havertz past and Odegaard set a bit of a screen that stopped Lacroix getting close.

Former Chelsea player scores against former Arsenal goalkeeper. Interesting reaction from the Arsenal players to that Havertz goal: most of them ran straight back to their own half. They want to get on with this game. Suggests they can sense Chelsea’s vulnerability.

Against his former club, Havertz gets the equaliser but again there will be an offside check. It appears he is onside as he receives the ball on the right. Havertz then drives across the face of the penalty area and shoots towards the near post. Martinez should make the save but can only palm it into the corner of the net. The goal stands and it is 1-1 at the Emirates.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

I think we’d be talking about Robert Sanchez if he had let that Havertz shot in at his near post. That wasn’t great from Martinez and Arsenal fans will love reminding him of it. Great game, this.

James decides to shoot from range and he strikes it really well, forcing Raya into a good save. Arsenal then counter and it ends with Odegaard having a shot blocked. Should Havertz have shot himself rather than lay it off for Odegaard?

Back come Chelsea and Pedro nearly gets on the end of a cross from Palmer.

Palmer, who has been quiet so far, receives it on the edge of the box and he is afforded too much space. He decides to shoot and looks to curl it into the far corner but Raya gets down to his right to make the save. He had to make sure he did not spill it as Pedro was lurking.

Tzolis cross from the left having been found by a great ball from Odegaard finds Havertz near the edge of the box. Fofana makes a crucial block to deny Havertz but Arsenal have the corner out on the left. Once more, Chelsea leave plenty of players up the pitch and Fofana heads away.

Odegaard works it to Saka on the right side of the box and the latter strikes towards goal, forcing Martinez into a decent save.

The goal will not stand. Konsa was offside before Calafiori scored so Chelsea remain 1-0 up.

#ARSCHE – 12' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of goal – and determined that Konsa was in an offside position in the build-up and recommended that the goal was disallowed.

The hosts equalise with a set-piece. Pedro should clear Rice’s free-kick but completely misses it. The ball comes to Gabriel, whose shot is saved by Martinez. Konsa then hits the post before a mad scramble ensues. Calafiori then forces the ball into the net. However, VAR are checking the goal...

Hato brings Saka down not far outside the Chelsea penalty area and both Odegaard and Rice are standing over it. Chelsea have just three men in the wall. Rice is going to take...

Arsenal have a corner out on the right yet Chelsea, who are the ones defending, leave four players up the pitch rather than in their own box. Is that madness or a masterstroke? The delivery from Saka goes beyond the back post, where it is then headed back across goal. Saka gets to it and then goes down but he was offside anyway.

It looked like Chelsea left four attackers upfield for that Arsenal corner. That’s one way of reducing the traffic in the six-yard box.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first five minutes of each of their three Premier League games this season. Has that ever happened before? Thanks OptaJoe:

Fofana brings down Havertz with a rather silly challenge and Arsenal have a free-kick out on the right, with the chance to send it into the Chelsea box. Odegaard drills it low in towards the near post and picks out the run of Calafiori. The Italian’s effort is saved by Martinez’s legs and then a mad scramble for the ball ensues. It is difficult to see where the ball is and ends up going out for a goal kick. Martinez stays down and is receiving treatment to his head. It comes as a result of Gabriel’s boot flying into Martinez’s head. Should VAR be taking a look at that one? They clear it but Gabriel might count himself lucky that a review for violent conduct was not called.

Not even two minutes into the game, Chelsea take the lead and it is a man Arsenal wanted over the summer who scores against them. Rogers, on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area, watches the ball onto his foot and volleys first time into the bottom left corner. A fine finish from Rogers and Chelsea have the perfect start. After just two minutes. I’m also pretty sure Rogers imitated the Thierry Henry celebration next to the corner flag just to rub salt into Arsenal’s wounds.

The two bosses, who have known each other since they were children, share a warm embrace before kick-off.

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

#1856. Michael Carrick spotted ordering Man Utd star to leave the pitch after Roma win

Michael Carrick was spotted telling Matheus Cunha to leave the pitch immediately after the final whistle in Manchester United’s comeback victory over AS Roma.

The Brazil international scored twice as United fought back from two goals behind to win 3-2 at Old Trafford on Tuesday night. After Bruno Fernandes’ penalty, Cunha pounced on a defensive error to level the contest before firing home a winner on 86 minutes.

The former Wolves star removed his shirt and leapt into the crowd in celebration, earning himself a booking. A second yellow followed in injury time for an overzealous challenge as United held on.

Cunha slowly trudged around the perimeter of the pitch as he made his way to the tunnel, desperate to see the final minutes of the match play out.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

He briefly disappeared down the tunnel before reemerging to join the post-match celebrations after the final whistle had blown.

But TV cameras picked up Carrick appearing to tell his player to go straight to the dressing room with Cunha seen pleading with his boss on the pitch. The unhappy Brazilian eventually made his way back down the tunnel, flanked by a club official.

IFAB rules, which also govern Champions League matches, state that a player who has been sent off ‘must leave the vicinity of the field of play and the technical area’ and cannot return, even after the full-time whistle has been blown.

Cunha is set to miss United’s next Champions League match away to Sporting CP on 25 November.

Victory handed Carrick a lifeline with United’s focus now shifting to Aston Villa on Sunday.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At half-time, I was wanting them to be more positive, if anything, and not get too disappointed and frustrated,’ said Carrick.

‘When you keep trying to do something, the easiest thing is feeling sorry for yourself. If something goes wrong, you get disappointed. That’s not going to help anybody. We might as well all go home if that’s the case. We’ve got to keep looking for the next moment, the next solution.

‘I don’t like to keep talking to the lads about what this place can do and the history and what’s gone before too much, but it’s there.

‘This place does magical things, it’s done it before and it’ll do it over and over again at some point in the future. There’s just something in this place that when we do have these types of nights, we do it the hard way.

‘But one moment can flip the whole place in a different direction. I spoke about that with the boys. Let’s have one moment that can trigger it. And we had that.’

#1854. Real Sociedad vs Lyon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 13:29, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 13:31

The Anoeta Stadium will play host to a fascinating Europa League contest on Thursday, as Real Sociedad welcome Lyon in the league stage of the tournament.

Real Sociedad are currently 14th in the overall table, picking up four points from three matches, while Lyon are 12th, collecting six points from three games.

Real Sociedad were outstanding in their last Europa League fixture on October 22, recording a 6-0 victory over Lillestrom, with that result following a 2-1 home loss to Bournemouth and a 1-1 draw with Union SG in this season's league stage.

Four points from three games has left them in 14th spot in the division, and they have matches after this one against Crystal Palace, Torreense, Viktoria Plzen and Juventus.

Pellegrino Matarazzo's side will enter this match off the back of a 2-1 defeat to Athletic Bilbao in the Basque derby, so they will be fired-up to bounce back on Thursday.

The White and Sky Blues reached the last-16 stage of the Europa League in their last participation in the tournament in 2024-25, and it would be a surprise if they were unable to advance deep into this season's competition given their quality.

Real Sociedad have won three of their last four matches in all competitions, while their loss in the Basque derby on Sunday was their first defeat of any kind since September 17.

Lyon, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of a 2-0 win over Angers in Ligue 1, with that result following back-to-back defeats for the French club.

One of those losses came in the team's last European fixture, going down 3-0 against Hoffenheim on October 22, with that result coming after a 3-2 success over Crystal Palace.

Paulo Fonseca's side also won their opening match in this season's Europa League league stage, beating Anderlecht 2-1, so six points have been gathered from three matches, which has left them in 12th spot in the division ahead of the next round of fixtures.

Lyon reached the last-16 stage of the 2025-26 Europa League, going out of the competition to Celta Vigo, while they made the quarter-finals in 2024-25, losing to Manchester United.

Les Gones will also take on Lillestrom, Union SG, Jagiellonia and Bayer Leverkusen before the league stage of the Europa League draws to a close.

Real Sociedad will be without the services of Luken Beitia, Alvaro Odriozola and Arsen Zakharyan through injury on Thursday night.

Luka Sucic is actually the team's leading goalscorer this season, coming up with six goals in 13 appearances, and he is set to continue in the final third of the field.

Meanwhile, there will be a start in the attack for Spain's World Cup winner Mikel Oyarzabal.

As for Lyon, Nicolas Tagliafico, Mohamed Ouedraogo, Tyler Morton, Pavel Sulc and Lois Openda are out of the European fixture due to injury problems.

Noah Nartey has been a standout performer for Lyon this season, coming up with two goals from midfield, and the 21-year-old will be in the starting side.

There is also expected to be a spot in an attacking area for Keito Nakamura.

Michael Carrick’s struggling side came from 2-0 down to clinch an unlikely 3-2 win over Serie A side Roma at Old Trafford.

Manchester United, enduring their worst start to a season since the 1980s, went behind after just 11 minutes as Matias Soule took advantage of space left by the absent Dalot to fire past Senne Lammens.

Dalot was out of position again five minutes later as Ayden Heaven blocked a shot with his arm to give Roma a penalty which was converted by Donyell Malen.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The home side were once again booed off and Michael Carrick was surely heading for the sack until United produced a brilliant second-half comeback.

Bruno Fernandes got the Red Devils back in the game with a retaken penalty won by Matheus Cunha, who then scored two late goals to stun the Italians and spark bedlam at Old Trafford.

O’Hara praised Manchester United’s unlikely comeback but said the team were ‘pathetic’ in the first-half and was particularly critical of ‘atrocious’ Portugal international Dalot.

‘We were watching the Manchester United game and the first-half was pathetic, we were in shock at how bad they were,’ O’Hara said on talkSPORT.

‘They could have been 4-0 down. But in the second half they turned it around and they were fantastic, they put in a big performance in the end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But they were pathetic in the first-half, it was so open and they stopped running, they had given up. They were gone, they were done.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/DtIOFJYZ6D

‘Roma should have absolutely buried them but they didn’t. They were all over the place at the back. Dalot… oh my god.

‘I said during the first-half, they have to take him off, he was atrocious. I don’t know what he was doing, I don’t know. It was awful defending, it was so bad. I couldn’t believe how bad they were.’

Carrick praised his players for their response in the second-half and urged them to take that momentum into United’s dismal Premier League campaign.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United are just 17th in the top-flight, two points above bottom-placed Sunderland, ahead of Sunday’s clash against Aston Villa.

‘It was a good night,’ Carrick told Amazon Prime. ‘I have to give credit to the players, I think we grew into it after giving the goals away.

‘The boys made every little bit of every opportunity. We were brilliant in the end. It’s one game though, it depends what happens next and we have to show that.

‘It’s a win for us as a football club and we get to send the fans home happy. We have to make the most of it. I don’t have a crystal ball to know what happens next.

‘We move on to the weekend. We’ve got a really important game here against Aston Villa, which we need to prepare for right.’

Meanwhile, Manchester United captain Fernandes said the win was not about saving Carrick his job.

‘We don’t need to save anyone’s job,’ he insisted. ‘The club needed that win, the players needed that win.

‘We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together. It’s been tough but it doesn’t change the belief I have of the manager and the staff and every player in this club.

‘It doesn’t change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me.’

United’s next opponents Aston Villa are 10th in the Premier League and lost 3-0 to Champions League contenders Barcelona on Tuesday night.

#1849. Jesus de Miguel: Kylian Mbappe, Pedri lead tributes to Tenerife striker following death aged 30

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 13:49

The footballing world was rocked by unimaginable tragedy on November 3, when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel Alameda died at the age of 30 following a collision with an opposing goalkeeper.

De Miguel and FC Andorra shot-stopper Jesus Owono both charged down a long ball towards the end of a Segunda Division match on Monday, and the latter's knee collided with the former's face and chest.

Distressed players from both teams immediately called for medical attention, and De Miguel was immediately taken to hospital, where his condition was reported as serious but stable.

However, De Miguel devastatingly deteriorated overnight, and the forward lost his life in the early hours of Tuesday morning following a cardiac arrest.

De Miguel's death sparked an outpouring of tributes from across the globe, as players, clubs, organisations, member associations and high-ranking officials all offered their support to the late striker, his family, his friends and his club.

Rotos de dolor, con un nudo en la garganta y sin poder creer que esto sea verdad, desde el CD Tenerife comunicamos el trágico fallecimiento, este martes, día 3 de noviembre de 2026, a las 8:00 horas, de Jesús de Miguel Alameda. No hay palabras de consuelo; no hay absolutamente nada que mitigue este sentimiento repleto de tristeza. Estamos junto a su desolada familia, junto a sus seres queridos, junto a todo el tinerfeñismo que hoy llora por este cruel desenlace. La familia de Jesús de Miguel agradece todas y cada una de las muestras de apoyo recibidas, e igualmente solicita, de corazón, máximo respeto a su privacidad, en estos terribles momentos. ? DEP

Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe took to Instagram with the statement "So sad, there are no words. Rest in peace", while his former Paris Saint-Germain teammate Achraf Hakimi posted on X: "A hug to all your loved ones. Rest in peace."

Meanwhile, Barcelona midfielder Pedri wrote on social media: "The death of Jesus de Miguel leaves me speechless. A huge hug for his family and the Tenerife family. And a heartfelt and respectful remembrance for him. Rest in peace."

Ex-Barcelona, Chelsea and Spain winger Pedro described De Miguel's loss as "irreplaceable", saying: "Deeply saddened by the passing of Jesús. All my love and affection to his family and friends for this irreplaceable loss. A big hug to everyone in Tenerife."

La Liga president Javier Tebas reposted Tenerife's original statement on X, saying: "Deeply saddened by the passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, player of CD Tenerife.

"Today we all share the terrible pain of an irreparable loss. My deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, teammates, and his entire club. All my affection and support in these such difficult moments. Rest in peace."

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa also expressed his condolences, saying: ""All my affection and my deepest condolences to the family of Jesus, to his loved ones, and to all of tinerfenismo. Rest in peace."

Among those to reply to Tenerife's social media statement were David de Gea, who posted a broken heart and prayer emoji, and Gerard Pique, who wrote "I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesus."

Real Madrid defender Eder Militao responded: "Sad day for football. Strength to all their family and friends", while Aymeric Laporte wrote "DEP" for descanse en paz, which translates to rest in peace.

Formerly of the Leganes youth academy, De Miguel exclusively spent his professional career in the lower leagues of Spanish football, as well as making a handful of Copa del Rey appearances.

The 1996-born striker moved to Tenerife in the summer of 2025 and was a key player in their successful promotion bid from the third tier in 2025-26, scoring 11 goals and providing seven assists in 29 league matches.

Miguel had previously represented Castellon in the Segunda Division and also played for Unionistas CF, CDA Navalcarnero, CF Fuenlabrada, AD Union Adarve and Internacional de Madrid.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Dejan Kulusevski has been called up by Sweden ahead of the November international break as the Tottenham playmaker continues his recovery from a long-term kneecap injury.

Kulusevski has not played for Sweden since suffering the injury while playing for Spurs in May 2025.

Spurs will continue to be cautious with the former Juventus man, but his inclusion in Graham Potter’s Sweden squad for the upcoming international break represents another step forward.

#1844. Celtic vs Besiktas - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 03 Nov 2026 14:48, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 15:02

Celtic's search for their first point in the Europa League league phase resumes when they welcome Besiktas to Celtic Park on Thursday.

The hosts are 35th in the table after three consecutive defeats, while the visitors are eighth and unbeaten after three matches.

Celtic have experienced a 2026-27 packed with inconsistent spells, underwhelming performances and subpar results, particularly in European competition.

The Bhoys catastrophically failed to qualify for the Champions League after squandering a 4-0 lead against LASK Linz to lose 5-4 on aggregate, marking one of the most miserable nights in the club's modern memory.

Martin O'Neill's side were subsequently demoted to the Europa League, where their misery has continued, with Celtic currently sitting 35th in the 36-team table with no points after three straight defeats.

Alongside their disastrous Europa League form, which has seen them concede nine goals and score just three times in three games, Celtic also head into Thursday's match off the back of another disappointing defeat at the weekend.

Celtic were handed a 2-0 loss by Falkirk on Sunday, marking the sixth defeat in their last 10 matches across all competitions, alongside only three wins during that time.

As the pressure continues to rise on O'Neill, the manager will be desperate for his side to bounce back from Sunday's defeat and secure their first points of the 2026-27 Europa League campaign.

However, Celtic will take on a Besiktas side that remain undefeated in the league phase thus far, having claimed two wins and one draw from their three fixtures.

Vincenzo Italiano's side claimed a particularly notable 4-1 triumph over Marseille on matchday one, followed by a 3-2 win against Hoffenheim and 2-2 draw with Crystal Palace, leaving them eighth in the standings with seven points.

While they remain unbeaten in this competition, Besiktas have endured an inconsistent recent run of results in the Turkish Super Lig, with two wins, two defeats and a draw in their last five.

All three times Besiktas have dropped points during that run came when playing away from home, while they have actually won only four of their nine away games across all competitions this season.

Despite their struggles on the road, Besiktas will be confident of capitalising on Celtic's defensive vulnerabilities in the Europa League, with the Bhoys conceding nine times in three games and the visitors scoring nine in their three league phase fixtures.

Celtic are contending with injury issues to Alistair Johnston and Yang Hyun-Jun, while the remainder of the squad should be available for selection.

After suffering a 2-0 defeat to Falkirk last time out, O'Neill could decide to make numerous changes to the starting 11 for this game, meaning the likes of Kasper Hogh, Sebastian Tounekti and Benjamin Nygren could start.

Meanwhile, the visitors will be without Orkun Kokcu and Fabio Miretti due to injuries, with Umit Akdag also unavailable after receiving a red card in the draw with Crystal Palace.

Dusan Vlahovic is Besiktas' top scorer in the Turkish Super Lig with seven goals, and the striker is likely to lead the line and continue his search for a first goal in the Europa League.

#1843. Rafa Benitez sends clear advice to Unai Emery over Man Utd job

Unai Emery should reject Manchester United and continue with Aston Villa if he receives an offer to take charge at Old Trafford.

That’s the view of former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who has warned Emery that the grass isn’t always greener amid speculation linking his fellow Spaniard with the United job.

There had been optimism amongst United’s fanbase after Michael Carrick was appointed on a full-time basis in the summer having led the Red Devils to an impressive third-place finish.

But just six months on and Carrick’s future has been plunged into doubt after what has been a wretched start to the new campaign, with United languishing down in 17th in the Premier League table – only two points better off than rock-bottom Sunderland.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

A thrilling comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League brought the club’s miserable nine-match winless streak to a halt on Tuesday night, easing some of the pressure on Carrick.

However, United’s overall performance was bordering on diabolical for much of the first half and questions over Carrick’s position will intensify again should his side suffer a further setback at home to Villa this weekend.

Sunday’s contest has been billed as a potential managerial audition for Emery, the man in the opposition dugout, who has worked wonders across his four-year spell at Villa Park.

According to Benitez, though, Emery should think very carefully before leaving a club where he has universal ‘support’ to join a club where he may not be given the same backing.

Asked if his compatriot should jump ship if he received a call from United, Benitez told talkSPORT: ‘I had six years at Liverpool, three at Newcastle, six months at Chelsea and not so much at Everton.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But I can tell you that if you’re at a club where they support you, they give you almost everything that you need, you can build something and Unai is already doing that.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘So I think it is a time for him to continue doing that and later on see.

‘In a couple of years, if he cannot get what he wants, his aspirations or his targets, maybe he has to consider other things.

‘But to find now an owner, the fans, everybody loves you, and then they give you support, it’s quite difficult to find.’

Benitez thinks Emery does not get the credit he deserves in their native Spain despite the extraordinary success the 55-year-old has achieved with Sevilla, Villarreal and now Villa.

‘The reality is that in Spain we don’t praise our people. We’re used to praising people coming from abroad,’ he added.

‘So if you are building something then it’s, “Okay, fine”, and then you go abroad and win something and people consider you a legend.

‘It happens a lot in Spain, it’s one of our big problems in Spain.’

Speaking to Amazon Prime after United’s Champions League epic with Roma, Carrick took the opportunity to praise the character his players displayed to come back from two goals down and emerge victorious.

However, he was also keen to stress that the win would only mean something if they were able to back it up on a consistent basis, with games coming thick and fast over the winter period.

‘It’s one game so it depends on what happens next. We’ve got to capitalise on that, but the boys showed an awful lot in the second half.

‘This was right at that moment. It depends on what happens next. We’ve got to make the most of it, we’ve got to move forward, but I’m feeling a lot better about things.

‘It’s a win for us as a football club. To see the supporters go home happy is what we live for, to give them performances and nights like this so they can get back energised again.

‘As a team, we’ve shown a lot of character to weather what we’ve had to. You find out a lot about each other.

‘The players will find out things about me, I certainly do about them and their character, what it means to them and what they’re prepared to put in.’

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

#1841. Paul Merson makes JJ Gabriel claim as Man Utd youngster agrees to join Real Madrid

Paul Merson says Manchester United will be ‘gutted’ to lose JJ Gabriel to Real Madrid as he ‘could have been a superstar’ at Old Trafford.

The 16-year-old has reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid in January after walking out on United earlier in the season.

Gabriel, who was branded the ‘best 15-year-old in Europe’ last year, was expected to become Manchester United’s youngest player in the Carabao Cup in September.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Bernabeu bosses have not contacted United to discuss the situation but Gabriel, who turned 16 last month, has verbally agreed to join Real Madrid in January.

Merson believes Manchester United will be ‘gutted’ to lose such a top talent but understands Gabriel’s desire to play for Madrid.

‘This kid’s a good player,’ the former Arsenal and England winger told Sky Sports. ‘He’s a very good player.

‘He could have been a superstar so Manchester United will be gutted. I think this rule’s got to change. I think it’s because his mum and dad have got an Irish passport that he’s allowed to go abroad.

‘And I think that needs to change. Manchester United have worked on this kid, made him the player he is. Obviously, he’d have been gifted at the same time.

#1840. Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool: Reds stunned in Istanbul to lose perfect Champions League record

Even Liverpool’s multi-million pound bench could not rescue a team floundering in Istanbul as a chaotic performance was punished by Fenerbahce as they twice came from behind to win 3-2.

Alexander Isak had scored within three minutes of coming on to put the visitors ahead going into the final quarter but, like in the first half, the lead lasted just four minutes before former West Brom trainee Archie Brown equalised courtesy of some lax defending.

But worse was to follow as Vedat Muriqi outjumped three players to nod in the winner and end Liverpool’s 100 per cent record.

And while Andoni Iraola will be scrutinised for making five changes, including resting three of his front four in Sunday’s defeat to Arsenal, it was the way the team lost their cool and control in a game they had in hand which was more damaging.

It was a harsh result on 19-year-old Trey Nyoni, who belied his relative inexperience with a composed performance capped by an excellent volley to open the scoring, becoming Liverpool’s youngest player to register his maiden goal in the Champions League and second-youngest scorer in the competition after Trent Alexander-Arnold.

But Liverpool’s Turkish troubles continued – they lost twice to Galatasaray last season – on a typically fractious night in Istanbul, with former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood scoring the first equaliser with a free-kick which deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet.

Arsenal XI vs Slavia Prague: Starting lineup and confirmed team news

They had been in total command up to that point but from there the game descended into something more manic, which suited a team hammered 6-0 at Villa Park last month and stoked a febrile home crowd.

Many of Liverpool’s players did not cope well in that atmosphere but, to his immense credit, Nyoni shone.

Iraola’s choice to leave out Isak, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo as they come to the end of a run of nine games in 27 days was understandable but it left his side toothless.

Bradley Barcola was deployed as striker but his unfamiliarity with the role was evident after failing to properly anticipate Joe Gomez’s low cross to the near post.

He did flick one header wide but struggled with the physicality of Fenerbahce’s centre-backs, even though Kojo Oppong was making his first Champions League start.

There was a lot of naivety within the visitors’ ranks – Victor Munoz snatched at an early chance when he was found in acres of space before redeeming himself by eventually forcing Ederson into a save – but none of it came from Nyoni.

The teenager was composed on just his seventh Champions League appearance – with everything going through him at the base of midfield.

His use of the ball, tactical awareness and unshakeable belief in his own ability meant amid the hurly burly of a typically Turkish clash he was head and shoulders above everyone else.

Many of Liverpool’s players did not cope well in that atmosphere but, to his immense credit, Nyoni shone.

Even the usually unflappable Virgil van Dijk’s patience was tested, pushing Irfan Kahveci to the floor at a second-half corner, having twice had Romelu Lukaku leave something on him in the early stages.

When Liverpool’s breakthrough came it was fully deserved as Rio Ngumoha’s cross to the far post saw Van Dijk’s pressure force Brown to head weakly to the edge of the penalty area where Nyoni dispatched the dropping ball via a deflection off Oppong.

But after a sliding Kahveci smashed against the crossbar from five yards, Greenwood’s free-kick went through the wall.

Isak headed in Gakpo’s cross with his first chance after those two and Wirtz were summoned in the 66th minute, but the unmarked Brown tapped in the equaliser and more poor defending saw Muriqi head home the winner.

#1838. AC Milan vs Ferencvaros - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 03 Nov 2026 15:12, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 15:15

One of five teams still with maximum points in the Europa League, Hungarian giants Ferencvaros will put that perfect record on the line when they visit AC Milan on Thursday.

Though Milan celebrated a domestic derby win at San Siro last time out, they are at risk of making an early exit from Europe.

Seven-time European champions, Milan were humbled by modest Bournemouth in their last Europa League match, falling behind within a few minutes before seeing their captain sent off.

Without Mike Maignan, the Rossoneri went on to lose 3-0 on England's south coast, leaving them on three points from as many league-phase games.

Ruben Amorim had started with defeat to his old club Benfica, before recording a 4-0 victory in Salzburg, so his side certainly have some work left if they are to qualify for the knockout rounds.

It has been an eventful fortnight since Milan were picked off by the Cherries: first, they beat free-falling Udinese 2-0, then they suffered another midweek meltdown.

Amorim's unbeaten domestic record finally ended in a chaotic encounter at San Siro, which finished 4-2 to Bologna, and that was far from ideal preparation for the Derby della Madonnina.

Yet, the rampant Rossoneri surged into a two-goal lead over Inter on Saturday night, before their old foes pulled one back; then, as half time approached, Diego Moreira's stunning free-kick essentially put the result beyond doubt.

So, having closed within four points of their city rivals, Milan sit fifth in Serie A and are still in what could be a multi-club title race.

While Milan lie 24th in the Europa League table - occupying the final playoff place as things stand - Ferencvaros may be eyeing automatic entry to the last 16.

Hungary's most successful club currently sit fourth with maximum points, following a home win over Portuguese second-tier side Torreense last month.

Though they were level at half time, second-half strikes from Mariano Gomez and Krisztian Lisztes - scored either side of an own goal - saw Fradi stroll to a 4-1 victory.

After previously beating Celtic and Viktoria Plzen, Balazs Borbely's men are very much in contention to make the top eight, which would help them skip the precarious playoff round.

Incidentally, the last time Ferencvaros won four consecutive matches in major UEFA competition was way back in the 1967-68 campaign, when they posted six straight wins en route to the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup final.

Given recent results, Borbely's squad might hope to emulate that run: including all domestic games and four rounds of Europa League qualifying, they have only lost once this season.

Sunday's 2-0 victory over Paks left them just two points behind Hungarian league leaders - and reigning champions - ETO Gyor, but Fradi have one game in hand.

After the Milan derby and before Sunday's trip to Genoa, Amorim is set to rotate his squad, with players such as Alphadjo Cisse being promoted from the bench.

The young forward - who scored a hat-trick versus Salzburg and a brace against Bologna - could join Omari Hutchinson and Davide Bartesaghi in a reshuffled lineup.

As Maignan must serve a suspension for his red card against Bournemouth, Lorenzo Torriani should deputise in goal.

Injured quintet Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Mattia Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek are still unavailable, while Filippo Terracciano remains a doubt.

Ferencvaros will be missing Slovakia midfielder Matus Bero, and Bence Otvos has yet to complete his recovery from an ACL injury.

Up front, Kristoffer Zachariassen (three goals, one assist) and Dele Yusuf (two goals, two assists) both aim to extend a fine start to the league phase.

The pair also notched one goal apiece last weekend; Serbian winger Veljko Birmancevic should join them in the final third.

Torriani; Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Bartesaghi; Hutchinson, Musah, Jashari, Cisse; Pulisic, Ramos

Radnoti; O. Nagy, Zohore, Gomez, O'Dowda; Maiga, A. Nagy; Arzani, Zachariassen, Birmancevic; Yusuf

Under pressure to collect all three points on home turf, Milan may struggle to beat Ferencvaros, whose last loss dates back to the end of July.

Nonetheless, Fradi face an altogether new challenge at the historic San Siro, where Amorim's men have begun to shown signs of promise.

#1837. Goalkeeper Jesus Owono issues first statement after death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is enduring ‘the most difficult days of my life’ following the death of the Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 30-year-old died in hospital on Tuesday following a challenge from Owono during FC Andorra’s game against Tenerife in the Spanish second division on Monday.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono had sprinted from his goal towards the halfway line and struck the Tenerife striker in the chest with his knee as he attempted to clear the ball.

After being taken to hospital, Tenerife described De Miguel’s condition as ‘stable’ on Monday night but the club issued a second update in the early hours of Tuesday morning which said that his ‘medical condition has deteriorated neurologically.’

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

De Miguel died later on Tuesday morning, while police in Spain have opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter.

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono says he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

‘I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The club added at the end of the statement: ‘FC Andorra requests the utmost sensitivity and respect.’

On Tuesday, Owono received support from his national team, Equatorial Guinea, following De Miguel’s death.

Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, said: ‘I feel it is necessary to convey our full solidarity and support at this time to our player, Jesus Lazaro Owono.

‘We know that, as an involuntary participant in this fatal incident during the match, he is experiencing this situation with profound distress and anguish.

‘The Equatorial Guinean Football Federation offers him our full personal and professional support, fully aware of the severity of this event—something no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.

‘We share in your mourning and remain entirely at your disposal. Please accept our deepest respect and support during these most difficult times.’

FC Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz, who helped carry De Miguel off the pitch on a stretcher, also defended Owono, insisting his teammate would ‘never intentionally hurt anyone’.

‘There are moments when football stops making sense. Moments that stay with you forever and make you realise just how fragile life can be. What we have experienced is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely heartbroken, speechless and with a sadness that is difficult to put into words,’ Spatz wrote on Instagram.

‘First of all, I would like to express my most sincere condolences and send all my love to the family, friends and loved ones of Jesus, as well as to the entire Chicharrera fanbase and the football community.

‘Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

‘I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who has been deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know what kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

‘In football, accidents happen, but nobody could ever imagine that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn’t matter. All that matters is standing together in grief, showing the utmost respect and sending all our strength to the family and everyone suffering from this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.’

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal survived a late goal to beat Slavia Prague 2-1 and continue their strong start in the Champions League.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after charging through on goal in behind and Viktor Gyokeres, who assisted that opener, then got on the scoresheet himself with a wonderful curled finish.

At that stage the Gunners were cruising, but they dropped off significantly in the second half and allowed Slavia to grow in confidence and get back into the game.

Wiktor Nowak scored in the 90th minute as Slavia threatened a grandstand finish but Arsenal did enough to hold on and move up to third in the league-phase standings.

Here is how Matt Verri rated the Arsenal players...

Bit too casual at times with the ball, as he tried to keep himself interested on a very routine night. Did his best to preserve Arsenal’s clean sheet with a truly outrageous save with his fingertips late in the match, but got done with a teasing cross in stoppage-time.

Looked close to his best in attack, flying forward to support Madueke. Perfect cut-back should have been finished by Merino. Bullied Sturm when called into action defensively too. Sloppier after the break as Arsenal’s standards dipped.

City had taken the lead with an own goal from Castello Lukeba but the hosts quickly levelled through Ridle Baku.

#1828. Three players who could become Scott Parker's first West Ham signings in January, including £18m striker

By Lewis Blain | 03 Nov 2026 15:40

Scott Parker is expected to take charge of West Ham United after Nuno Espirito Santo was dismissed following a disappointing start to the Championship campaign.

The former Hammers midfielder faces the task of getting his former club back into the promotion picture, with the London Stadium outfit currently eighth and six points behind league leaders Middlesbrough.

West Ham initially looked capable of running away with the title after scoring 16 goals during a four-match winning streak in September, but they have since managed only two league victories in six outings. Consecutive home defeats to Southampton and West Bromwich Albion have ultimately cost Nuno his job.

Parker will inherit a squad that has undergone significant changes since relegation, with around £150m raised through player sales and some of that money reinvested in new arrivals.

However, the Hammers still have weaknesses to address, particularly in attack, and January could provide the new head coach with an opportunity to reshape his squad.

Sports Mole takes a look at three realistic names who could be among Parker's first signings in east London.

A striker should be near the top of Parker's shopping list, with Pablo and Taty Castellanos managing just two league goals between them in West Ham's opening 13 matches. Their combined six goal contributions are hardly convincing, particularly when centre-back Konstantinos Mavropanos has scored five times himself.

Abraham could offer a much-needed alternative, having struggled to secure regular opportunities since returning to Villa Park for around £18m in the summer. The 28-year-old was reportedly close to joining Ipswich Town on loan, but a move to West Ham could appeal given his previous success in the capital, where he scored 30 goals in 82 appearances for Chelsea.

The 11-time England international also has an impressive Championship record, finding the net 48 times in 78 appearances at that level.

With Nicolas Jackson and teenage prospect Brian Madjo seemingly ahead of him at Villa, Parker could offer Abraham the regular football he needs while gaining a proven goalscorer.

Another area requiring attention is the wide positions, particularly with Parker likely to favour his preferred 4-2-3-1 system. Manor Solomon has arrived to provide an attacking threat, but additional competition could help West Ham become more dangerous from the flanks.

Sancho remains without a club after leaving Manchester United in the summer, and the Irons have been linked with the former Borussia Dortmund star for several months. Reports suggest his representatives have contacted several English clubs, including the Hammers, to explore potential opportunities.

His Premier League record of 12 goals and 13 assists in 112 appearances is hardly spectacular, and there would understandably be reservations about taking a gamble on him. However, with no transfer fee required, Sancho could be a relatively low-cost opportunity for Parker to revive a player who has previously demonstrated considerable ability.

West Ham may also need to strengthen at centre-back, particularly with Mavropanos attracting reported interest from Turkish giants Besiktas following an encouraging start to the campaign.

Losing the Greece international would be a significant setback, especially given his importance to the defence, but it could force Parker to revisit an existing target. Rav van den Berg has been linked with the Hammers in recent windows, having cost FC Koln around £11m in 2025.

Parker would have encountered the former Middlesbrough defender during his time managing Burnley in the Championship, potentially giving him a useful understanding of his qualities.

With youngster Airidas Golambeckis already being asked to step into the first team, another centre-back would make sense even if Mavropanos stays.

A January move could therefore address a potential departure while adding a young defender with Championship experience.

#1827. Cardinale: “Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there”

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale spoke to CBS Sports before the derby win over Inter, pledging to bring the club back to the summit of football.

On Halloween night, the Rossoneri ensured that Inter’s derby nightmare continued as Milan won their fourth consecutive victory in the fixture, extending the unbeaten run against the Nerazzurri to eight meetings in the process.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

All of the damage was done in the first half. Christian Pulisic struck in the fourth minute with a header, Adrien Rabiot scored from a corner six minutes later, Alessandro Bastoni halved the deficit and then Diego Moreira converted a lovely free-kick to reopen the two-goal advantage.

In the end, 3-1 is how it would stay, securing a memorable win. Cardinale spoke with the CBS panel in the build-up to kick-off at San Siro last night and he shed a bit more light on his plans for the Rossoneri moving forward. His words are via MilanNews.

“Well, first of all, this stadium… As an American, I can say that a stadium like this is something you never see anywhere else. Tonight, it’s going to light up. There’s something different about this derby tonight than in the past.

“There’s an electricity here that I’ve never felt before. You’ll see nearly 80,000 people literally shaking this structure. It’s going to be truly incredible.”

“It is. You know, when we bought the club four years ago, I started working on this right away. And part of what we’re trying to do here is bring the best of America to Italian soccer, and specifically to AC Milan.

“It’s extraordinary: most people didn’t think we could accomplish all this, or even get to this point. Not only did we announce the stadium this week, but we also announced the largest naming rights deal in history. I think it’s a wonderful thing for Italian soccer.

“The message to everyone is that we’re coming back. Italian soccer truly deserves to be at the top again, and we’ll do everything we can through AC Milan to make that happen.”

“There’s a connection between us. We’re two guys from Pennsylvania trying to make their way and understand Italy. He’s ‘Captain America’, but he’s also my franchise player. I couldn’t be more thrilled to have him with us.

“It’s a true partnership with him. He’s a leader, and his presence on the court makes all the difference in the world. You’ve seen it this year: when he steps on the court, he completely changes the game.”

Why is AC Milan and winning with Milan so important to you?

“I remember George Steinbrenner telling me about twenty years ago, ‘Don’t get too emotionally involved in all this; don’t go into the locker room, don’t do those things’. But in this case, I got emotionally involved.

“For me, it became a personal issue. And I don’t know what it is: maybe it’s just that… look around, listen. This means so much to the people of Milan, it has a huge impact on them, and I feel a huge responsibility.

“AC Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there. This will probably be one of the greatest things I’ll do in my career.”

“It’s something multigenerational. This stadium is an icon. Look around, look at these people: this means everything to them. All of this carries with it an enormous amount of responsibility, it almost makes your wrists tremble.

“The best thing I can do is do my job well to help this club win, because victory spreads to the whole community. Listen… can you hear? That’s the Curva. You don’t see anything like it in America, it’s truly special.”

What’s your favourite detail of the new stadium?

“What we tried to do with the new stadium was to live up to the name and tradition of this facility. This is San Siro, but it is also ‘La Scala del Calcio’, the opera house of football.

“When you look at the design of the new stadium, those majestic, slender lines on the exterior recall the grand drapes and curtains of La Scala. It is our tribute to the history of this city.”

How did you manage to unblock the stadium situation?

“It’s been an incredible collaboration, a true partnership with our president Paolo Scaroni and the mayor. It’s extraordinary because everyone told me it’s impossible to build a stadium here in Italy. The last major stadium built in Italy was in 2011 in Turin, with about 40,000 seats.

“The extraordinary thing about our project is that it will be a 75,000-seat stadium, and we expect to have it completed before the 2032 European Championships. It will be a great thing for all of Italy.”
