#1807. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Sep 8: Club Brugge vs Aston VillaOct 14: Aston Villa vs Fenerbahçe Oct 21: Aston Villa vs Viking Nov 3: Barcelona vs Aston VillaNov 24: Galatasaray vs Aston Villa Dec 8: Aston Villa vs Paris St-Germain Jan 19: Aston Villa vs Borussia DortmundJan 27: Slavia Praha vs Aston Villa

Quite the evening, last time out at the Jan Breydel Stadium 💫 pic.twitter.com/NogGLLSMFU

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1806. Sunderland experiencing the ‘most demanding challenge’ in their history, says Le Bris

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Regis Le Bris believes Sunderland are experiencing "the most demanding challenge in their history" as they try to fight on multiple fronts.

Sunderland finished seventh in their first season back in the Premier League, securing Europa League football for 2026-27.

They have struggled in the top flight this season, sitting bottom after the first nine matches with just one win to their name, but have made an unbeaten start to their European campaign (W2 D1) as well as reaching the EFL Cup quarter-finals.

Ahead of hosting Dinamo Zagreb in their fourth Europa League game, Sunderland have netted just four goals in the league phase, despite generating 7.7 xG in total – their -3.7 xG underperformance is currently the worst in the competition.

But they will not mind, given they sit ninth in the table and have lost just one of their seven major European competition matches in club history (W5 D1), a 2-0 away defeat to Sporting CP in November 1973 in the Cup Winners' Cup.

When asked if they were struggling to find the right balance across all competitions, Le Bris said their form is not a surprise.

"Growing pains. Is it unexpected? I would say no," he said. "We are experiencing probably the most demanding challenge Sunderland has ever faced in its history.

"Premier League, Europa League, quarter-final in Carabao Cup, FA Cup later. We earned it last season, and we are pleased to be in this position, but playing every three days is much more demanding than preparing for a game with one full week.

"It's a new journey – not for everyone, as many of our players have experienced this situation before – but it's still a new group.

"When you don't set the standards in one specific area in the Premier League, it's the Champions League, more or less, because every team is really strong, relentless, well-prepared, and you can't win.

"We are still competitive; we trust our team, our level. But repeating performances is different, and this is the next step."

Europa League mode: https://t.co/bgflTPSUYB

— Sunderland AFC (@SunderlandAFC) November 4, 2026

Sunderland's strong start in the Europa League includes wins over AZ and Torreense before their draw with Lech Poznan.

And Le Bris believes his side have coped with the gap in quality between the Premier League and Europe well.

"I think the gap is big, and it's positive for the Premier League, first of all," he added. "It shows the level.

"The difference between the bottom and top of the league is not so big, and it's really tight. So, for us, it means that every three days you have to reset, set the highest standards, and it's a new journey."

Sunderland host Dinamo Zagreb, who parted company with coach Mario Kovacevic earlier this week.

The Croatian side have won three of their last six European matches against English opposition (L3), this after winning just two of their first 16 combined.

#1805. Michael Carrick insists he will NOT be sacked as Man United manager - despite side slipping closer to relegation zone after Chelsea defeat

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER

Published: 12:33 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 12:50 EDT, 31 October 2026

Michael Carrick believes he will cling onto his job as Manchester United head coach despite watching helplessly as his team slid closer towards the relegation zone at Chelsea.

Goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer – who converted a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for picking up two yellow cards in the space of 82 seconds – consigned United to a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge as they sank to 17th(check) place in the Premier League.

Earlier this week, Carrick was given more time by Old Trafford bosses to turn the club’s disastrous season around, but he is now without a win in nine games.

Asked if he will be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Roma, he replied: ‘Yes. I'm just looking forward to getting the boys ready for the midweek now.’

The 20-time champions of England are faced with the humiliation of dropping into the bottom three and it was put to Carrick, a player and coach at United stretching back two decades, that seeing the club in such a position must be hurting him.

‘Yeah, pretty much exactly that,’ he said. ‘There is a lot of emotion. We're a great football club and we want to win football matches. Things have gone against us in a big way and unravelled quickly.

Man United are now without a win in nine games in all competitions, their longest such run since October-November 1988

‘There is no hiding from the fact that we haven't won enough games. There's no words that I'm going to explain to you now that makes it any different, it's not going to change it.

‘You can look at how far you can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches. So that's the way it's got to be approached, for sure.’

Carrick insisted that he didn’t feel let down by Martinez, but did not even look at the Argentine as he left the pitch.

‘It has a major importance on the game. A huge moment. I think that is pretty obvious really,’ added Carrick. ‘The second goal and losing the man at that stage had a big influence on it, for sure.’

The United fans continued to give Carrick their support while once again turning on the club’s owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso admitted Estevao’s positive performance will give him a selection headache after the wonderkid showed Chelsea what they have been missing.

Morgan Rogers' brilliant solo goal set Chelsea on their way to victory

The 19-year-old Brazilian was handed his first Premier League start of the season and scored two disallowed goals for offside as well as creating several other opportunities.

‘He’s given me reasons (to pick him),’ said Alonso. ‘This is football and sometimes you don’t get what you want, but the best way to show it is not by being angry, it’s by being competitive and Este has done it really well.’

Alonso also hailed Romeo Lavia after the 22-year-old Belgian filled in for the unwell Jordan Henderson in midfield on short notice, and was arguably this game’s best performer.

‘From a midfielder point of view, for me it has been a top, top performance,’ Alonso said. ‘He's done so many things right. He’s been always connecting the defence with the attacker players, he's been able to switch the game, he's taken many right decisions, he's been very dynamic, competitive. I'm very happy for him and he deserves a huge recognition for his performance.’

#1804. Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch suffers fracture as Andoni Iraola explains latest injury blow

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 17:18

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has offered further detail on the heel injury that has ruled Ryan Gravenberch out of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Fenerbahce.

On Tuesday morning, Liverpool released a statement announcing that the Netherlands international would be unavailable for the trip to Istanbul and would remain on Merseyside for treatment.

Gravenberch was an unused substitute during Liverpool's 1-0 Premier League loss to Arsenal on Sunday, which was originally believed to have been a selection decision from Iraola, who started Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni against the Gunners.

However, Gravenberch's demotion from the first XI was down to his new fitness issue, which Iraola confirmed in his pre-game press conference was a fracture of the heel.

The Liverpool boss conceded that Gravenberch has shown no improvement over the last 48 hours, although he did not rule him out of Sunday's Premier League clash with Crystal Palace.

“I don’t know, it’s a day-to-day thing," Iraola said when asked if Gravenberch could make the trip to Selhurst Park. "It’s a fracture of the heel. It’s about the pain.

"He has been with some discomfort. The other day against Arsenal he was warming up and he was not fully confident. He hasn’t improved since then.

“But it’s going to be something that every day we ask him, every day we see how he is. If he can be available for the weekend, lovely, he would be a very good help for us. But I cannot tell you right now."

Gravenberch played the full 90 in both of Liverpool's last two Champions League games against LASK Linz and Fenerbahce, and his absence could open the door for Nyoni to keep his place in the first XI.

The 19-year-old made his full Premier League debut in the loss to Arsenal, completing 59 minutes of the contest, after featuring for over 80 minutes against LASK and Villarreal.

Asked how big an opportunity Wednesday's game could be for Nyoni with Gravenberch out, Iraola added: "He has to continue in the same place he has been since the beginning of pre-season.

"He's playing most of the games, we trust him, he's doing very well. I think we have to encourage him to continue improving, continue learning, but he's in a very good place."

Dominik Szoboszlai is another midfield option for Liverpool after recovering from a hamstring injury, as the Reds aim to make it four wins from four in the 2026-27 Champions League.

Iraola's men are one of just five teams with nine points from their first three games and occupy third place in the Champions League table, only below Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain on goal difference.

#1803. GdS: An ‘achievable dream’ – why Cardinale left Italy ‘convinced’ by Scudetto bid

Gerry Cardinale left San Siro after the derby win over Inter with a distinct feeling: this AC Milan team can challenge for the title.

Happy as ever about the derby victory, yet still rueful over the defeat to Bologna – a stumble that must not be repeated – La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that Cardinale departed Italy yesterday, bound for New York, where his family and work await him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His thoughts however remain firmly fixed on AC Milan and the tasks that lie ahead, with the renewal of Adrien Rabiot’s contract as a short-term priority and the Scudetto as a cherished, long-term dream.

He admitted as much following the loss to Raffaele Palladino’s side, and he feels it even more strongly now, having won his first derby since taking direct personal control of the club on May 25th.

On Sunday evening, following the final whistle, Cardinale chose not to speak to the team. He had already said everything he needed to say to his players on Saturday at Milanello, aiming to motivate and spur them on to bounce back from the 4-2 defeat against Bologna.

The team took his words to heart: after the derby, Maignan and his team-mates could see the joy on Cardinale’s face, even though he didn’t utter a single word. Amorim, who granted the squad two days of (training set to resume tomorrow) offered his own praise for the team’s performance.

The head of RedBird Capital stepped away from the dressing room, wanting the moment to remain special for the players and the coaching staff, but also because he was deeply moved—tears nearly welling up in his eyes.

Milan, its fans, and the project itself all needed a night like this, and the American knew it. Now, however, Gerry expects the level of performance shown in the derby to be replicated in the upcoming matches, specifically the two before the break: Thursday against Ferencváros and Sunday in Genoa.

These are fixtures that will require managing the post-derby euphoria to ensure there is no drop in focus. While some of the squad celebrated at a well-known Milanese nightclub on Saturday night, the focus shifts to Europe starting tomorrow.

The position in the table needs to be improved following the slip-ups against Benfica and Bournemouth in the first three games. Beyond that, further progress will be required in Serie A.

The only way to close the seven-point gap on Lazio is to avoid any further stumbles like the one against Bologna. On this point, Cardinale and Amorim are in complete agreement.

In fact, while both were delighted by the triumph over their city rivals, that joy only sharpened their regret over the three points dropped against the Rossoblù. Neither the manager nor the owner could stomach the collapse from a 2-1 lead at halftime to a 4-2 defeat.

The two spoke after the derby and are fully aligned: injuries notwithstanding, a Milan side that aspires to be Milan once again – both in Italy and in Europe – cannot afford such lapses in focus.

Beating Inter is satisfying, and remaining unbeaten against their rivals for eight consecutive matches is a positive, but the ultimate priority remains lifting a trophy. City supremacy is not enough, not for Cardinale, and not for Amorim.

#1802. Crystal Palace vs Hoffenheim - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 03 Nov 2026 17:30, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 17:57

In need of a morale-boosting victory, out-of-sorts Crystal Palace welcome Hoffenheim to Selhurst Park for their latest League Phase fixture in the Europa League on Thursday night.

The Eagles sit 15th in the 36-team standings, while their German counterparts are eight places further back in 23rd spot after the first three rounds of fixtures.

After nine Premier League games, Crystal Palace find themselves languishing in the relegation zone having posted two wins, one draw and a joint division-high six defeats, leaving head coach Pierre Sage under increased pressure.

The Eagles, who have also conceded the most goals in the league (21), suffered their third straight top-flight loss last weekend as they were beaten 2-0 by Tottenham Hotspur, a result impacted by the 13th-minute dismissal of striker Jean-Philippe Mateta.

“A problem with performance” is what Sage clearly needs to address, and the Frenchman – appointed in June to succeed Conference League winner Oliver Glasner – now has two important home games against Hoffenheim and Liverpool to potentially save his job in South London.

Palace’s form in their maiden Europa League campaign has been mixed thus far; they thrashed Lech Poznan 4-0 at home on matchday one before losing 3-2 against Lyon and drawing 2-2 with Besiktas, away displays marked by sluggish starts and spirited yet flawed comeback attempts.

The Eagles will take some comfort from having won three of their last five home matches in all competitions (L2), while they also head into Thursday’s contest unbeaten in seven European games at Selhurst Park (W5 D2).

Competing in major European competition for just the fifth time in their history this season, Hoffenheim have accumulated only three points from a possible nine available at the start of their Europa League campaign (W1 L2).

Die Kraichgauer lost their opening two matches against OFI Crete (2-0) and Besiktas (3-2), but they achieved what Palace could not against Lyon, as they secured a convincing 3-0 victory over the French side a fortnight ago to open their account in the League Phase.

This statement win was part of a three-game winning streak for Christian Ilzer’s side across all competitions, but they have since been brought back down to earth by a DFB-Pokal second-round exit on penalties to Holstein Kiel and a 2-0 Bundesliga defeat against Werder Bremen, losing to the latter last Saturday.

Although five defeats in eight Bundesliga games has seen Hoffenheim slip down to 12th place in the table, already six points adrift of the top four, Ilzer has insisted that he is “not worried” about his team and has taken plenty of positives from their spirited performances.

Returning to winning ways on Thursday is not a given, though, as Hoffenheim have prevailed in only one of their last six European away games (D2 L3) while they have lost all five of their previous meetings with English opposition (once to Spurs, twice to Liverpool and Manchester City).

Crystal Palace trio Ismaila Sarr (groin), Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) and Chadi Riad (knee) all remain sidelined with injuries, but Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle) and Quinten Timber (hamstring) may be fit to return to the matchday squad.

Despite his Premier League red card, Mateta is available for selection on Thursday and will likely lead the line for the Eagles, with Yeremy Pino, Dwight McNeil, Eddie Nketiah, Dario Osorio and Evann Guessand all battling for starts in the final third.

Cheick Doucoure and Will Hughes are contenders to start in midfield, while Anan Khalaili and Ben Chilwell could both return as wing-backs at the expense of Oscar Mingueza and Tyrick Mitchell.

As for Hoffenheim, their packed treatment room includes ex-West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal, (thigh), Bambase Conte (adductor), Patrick Wimmer (hamstring), Valentin Gendrey (broken leg), Albain Hajdari (foot), Nathan De Cat (knee) and Max Moerstedt (head).

After missing the defeat at Werder Bremen through suspension, Alexander Prass is available to return and could feature as a central midfielder alongside either Leon Avdullahu or Wouter Burger.

Andrej Kramaric contributed to all three goals in the win against Lyon (one goal, two assists) and the 35-year-old will likely be joined in attack by Adam Daghim, Tim Lemperle and top scorer Adam Hlozek (four goals).

Ten of Hoffenheim’s 13 competitive games this season have produced over 2.5 goals, while each of Crystal Palace’s three Europa League matches this term has seen at least four goals scored, so an entertaining contest could be in store on Thursday.

Both teams are desperate for a victory to boost their knockout qualification hopes, but we can envisage the spoils being shared on this occasion.

#1801. Arbeloa encourages Fulham ‘to keep believing in the way that we are playing’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Alvaro Arbeloa has encouraged his Fulham side "to keep believing in the way that we are playing" ahead of their Premier League matchup against Newcastle United on Saturday.

After failing to win any of their first six league games this season (D2 L4), Fulham have bounced back with a three-game unbeaten run (W2 D1).

They followed up 1-0 wins over Hull City and Coventry City with a 1-1 draw with Aston Villa last time out.

Fulham accumulated 2.2 expected goals (xG) against Villa, but despite creating four Opta-defined 'big' chances, the Cottagers equalised with an own goal from Zion Suzuki.

Despite lacking a clinical edge in front of goal, Arbeloa believes his side are on the right path.

"I think I would be more worried if we don't create chances, but we are creating chances, so we need to keep believing in the way that we are playing," said Arbeloa.

"We need to keep working on our finishing. It's about creating chances, not conceding chances, and playing in the way that we believe, and I think we have done really well.

“We have a very difficult match [against Newcastle] on Saturday at home, and yes, we need to continue growing as a team, because we are just starting. I'm so happy and so proud of my players."

The month ahead.  https://t.co/rI8RDWaVDp

— Fulham Football Club (@FulhamFC) November 4, 2026

Newcastle are two points and two places above Fulham in 13th, but are struggling for form and confidence.

The Magpies have lost twice to Everton in their last two fixtures, first in the EFL Cup and then in the Premier League.

The Newcastle players were booed off at full-time after their league defeat to the Toffees at St. James' Park, and defender Dan Burn understood the fans' frustrations.

"When you're not winning games, there's always a lack of confidence," Burn told Sky Sports.

"The fans weren't happy. They have shown that at half-time and full-time. That doesn't make it easy to build confidence when you're in that atmosphere.

"But I've been a fan, so I understand the frustrations when they're not getting what they're expecting.

"It doesn't make it easier for us as players. You can sense that nervousness in the ground."

Fulham are responsible for two of the four players to have had the most touches in the opposition box in the Premier League this season: Josh King (57, first) and Oscar Bobb (50, fourth).

Of all players to have had 400+ touches this term, King has also had the highest share in the opposition box (13% – 57/438).

Yoane Wissa came on as a substitute in Newcastle's defeat to Everton and recorded the Magpies' only two shots on target.

He was responsible for 0.4 of their 1.3 xG, the most of any player, and was denied a goal following a superb save from Jordan Pickford.

Fulham have won three of their last four Premier League games against Newcastle (L1), having gone eight without a win against the Magpies beforehand (D2 L6).

None of the 18 Premier League meetings between Fulham and Newcastle in London have ended as draws (11 Fulham wins, seven Newcastle wins), with 16 played at Craven Cottage and two at Loftus Road (2002-03 and 2003-04).

No side from outside the capital have lost more Premier League games in London than Newcastle (97, level with Everton).

However, the Magpies have won both visits so far this season (2-0 v Tottenham and 2-0 v Crystal Palace), last winning more consecutively between May 2013 and January 2014 (four).

Newcastle are looking for consecutive away Premier League wins for the first time since March/April 2025 – each of their last four away wins in the competition have been in London.

#1799. Full throttle Brighton have the depth, quality and guile to hang in there with Arsenal and Man City, writes JACK GAUGHAN, as individual mistakes haunt Enzo Maresca's men in latest defeat

Published: 13:16 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 14:38 EDT, 31 October 2026

A game condensed into 15 seconds. Jeremy Doku loses possession on the touchline but won't have that, thundering into a tackle to recollect and then sets off beating two men. He seems in the mood for destruction.

An expectant Etihad is up, the Premier League's trickiest winger cutting loose and Manchester City are in. One calm final ball and an equaliser is on.

Doku tries to find a lurking Erling Haaland, or at least it appears so, because the pass is so bad that Brighton are already storming upfield themselves.

Around 15 minutes after that, Fabian Hurzeler is roaring at his bench. He is chest bumping substitutes and backroom staff with defiant pride, vindication of the words spoken about seeking revenge in the immediately aftermath of losing on penalties here in the cup a matter of days ago.

Brighton stayed in Manchester after Wednesday night and Hurzeler spent that time plotting, organising the battle plan to topple league leaders who have been fallible defensively under Enzo Maresca this season but are producing scintillating attacking moments.

Hurzeler leaves the north west following a little getaway at the Lowry Hotel having drawn and won against City over the course of two 90 minutes. His stock is soaring, his side a fascination and the faint chorus of 'we're gonna win the league' from the away end might just grow a little louder over the coming weeks if they can keep this up.

Manchester City were turned over by Brighton to make it back-to-back league defeats

Yasin Ayari's first half goal was all that was required for Brighton to leave as the victors

Brighton's manager peeled away from the group as they enjoyed being serenaded by the away end, instead sharing a moment with match winner Yasin Ayari, whose third goal of the campaign owed much to the quick thinking of Lewis Dunk to restart play from a dead ball with haste and the individual mistake of Matheus Nunes, failing to clear Diego Gomez's cross. Ayari and Dunk were those to miss from the spot in the Carabao Cup.

'Wednesday was brutal,' Hurzeler said. 'We promised ourselves that we won't have the same feeling.

'We created energy, positivity. How the players stuck together and built the connection through the four days is really impressive.'

Hurzeler discussed the virtue of luck here in midweek and City's was out on the day, now only two points between the teams after consecutive league defeats.

The joyous, and somewhat knowing, celebrations between staff members shone a light on the preparation that went into this result and how it quite clearly serves as a warning shot.

Brighton showed across four days that they have the depth, quality and wherewithal to be at least be considered strong enough to stay close with City and Arsenal. More specifically, they showed on Saturday that they can mix the way in which they play, adept to altering circumstances.

Their full throttle movement in midfield before half time confused their City counterparts, the home midfield discombobulated – arms pointing frantically, basic organisational shouts becoming more hurried – and that filtered through to other areas of the pitch.

Maresca was seem directing Elliot Anderson on who to follow and there were occasionally some befuddled looks.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was full stretch but could do nothing about Ayari's pinpoint strike

Enzo Maresca was in disbelief as his side spurned numerous opportunities to score a goal

Out of possession, home wingers were often full backs and full backs were often stationed as wingers as they followed their men, with Brighton happily piercing through any gaps. For a while, City were taken for a ride on the waltzers.

And then later on, when City pushed and pushed, Brighton went to a back six and contained.

They still gave up a number of very presentable chances, City failing to convert five of those – most notably two for Iliman Ndiaye and Nico O'Reilly's late header – but the rearguard action is proof that they own the minerals to enjoy more days like these before May is done.

Brighton managed to create four big chances from just nine touches inside the City box, indicating that once Maresca's midfield is breached then they are too easy to play through.

The Italian – who dropped Marc Guehi - is concerned by the volume of individual mistakes at both ends of the pitch after the Nunes error.

'We're probably conceding [too many] silly goals,' Maresca said, with the defeat at Aston Villa also pockmarked by them.

'We created enough but unfortunately didn't score. For sure we are not happy. Nobody is happy when we lose. But we were aware that we weren't going to win all the games.'

Maresca said he had not reviewed two penalty appeals for handball and the decision to award a free kick in the build up to Brighton's 11th-minute goal.

Brighton showed enough quality this week to suggest they can hang with Arsenal and Man City

Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 6; Nunes 5, Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Gvardiol 5 (Foden 79); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 6 (Cherki 55, 7); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 79), Fernandez 5 (O’Reilly 65), Doku 5; Haaland 5.

Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 7; Costinha 7, Vuskovic 7, Dunk 8, Boscagli 6 (Hadjam 64, 6); Gross 6, Chema 6 (Wieffer 64, 6); Gomez 7 (Rutter 84), Ayari 7, De Cuyper 7 (Yalcouye 72); Kostoulas 6 (Hinshelwood 72, 6).

Left back Josko Gvardiol was largely tucking in to become a third centre half and Nunes told to occupy the sort of attacking positions that the Croatian usually devours.

And interestingly, were City to win their appeal against the guilty verdicts – the sanctions for which would likely spell relegation – then left back is an area they would be expected to look at.

Sources have indicated that Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert is one potential target who was scouted extensively last season before City decided against bolstering their ranks in that area in the summer.

Rayan Ait-Nouri is looking to leave, while any signings in that position would present intrigue as to how Gvardiol and O'Reilly are used in future.

#1798. Fonseca leaves Lyon ahead of expected Sporting appointment

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Paulo Fonseca has left Lyon and is expected to become Sporting CP's new head coach.

Fonseca joined Lyon in January 2025 and led the club to a fourth-place finish in Ligue 1 last term, just missing out on Champions League football by a point.

This season, they sit third after nine games, having accrued 17 points (W5 D2 L2), and they sit just three points behind Ligue 1 leaders Paris Saint-Germain.

In total, Fonseca oversaw 82 matches in charge of the club, winning 46 of those games (D12 L24), and leaving with a win percentage of 56.1%.

While Sporting are yet to announce Fonseca's appointment, Lyon confirmed it in their announcement of his exit, also stating their disappointment over the 53-year-old's decision to leave.

"Approached in recent days by a club to which he is particularly attached, Paulo Fonseca has informed the management of his wish to leave Olympique Lyonnais," Lyon said in their statement.

"An unexpected decision which OL deeply regrets, all the more so by its timing in the middle of the season.

"Faced with this clearly expressed will, the management considered that it was not in the interest of the club to continue a collaboration that could no longer guarantee the level of total commitment essential to the success of the project.

"In such a decisive period of the season, Olympique Lyonnais believes that all of its forces must be fully mobilised and focused on the club's objectives.

"The management has therefore taken note of Paulo Fonseca's decision and is now working to identify his successor."

Official: Paulo Fonseca leaves OL to join Sporting CP. https://t.co/yjOtjLDEDR https://t.co/VGFHLy7luc

— Olympique Lyonnais (@OL_English) November 4, 2026

Sporting, who sacked Rui Borges on Monday after a poor start to their Primeira Liga campaign, will pay Lyon €5m in compensation for Fonseca's exit.

Fonseca is returning to his home country as a manager for the first time since leaving Braga in May 2016.

In a statement on social media, Fonseca addressed the Lyon fans, saying: "Some decisions in life are both sources of happiness and sadness. This one is part of that.

"I bid farewell to Olympique Lyonnais, and it's far more difficult than I ever could have imagined.

"Over time, Lyon has become much more than just a place where I worked: it has become a home. A place where I felt safe, supported, and respected, even in the most challenging moments. I will never forget that.

"To the supporters: thank you for making me feel at home. Your passion, your love for this club, and all the emotions we've shared will remain etched in my memory forever.

"Football has been part of my life for as long as I can remember. And sometimes, it offers you the chance to fulfil a dream you've carried since childhood. That moment has arrived for me. I am happy and grateful for what lies ahead, but a part of my heart will always remain in Lyon.

"I leave with immense gratitude and memories that I will cherish for the rest of my life. Thank you, Lyon. For everything."

#1796. CorSera: Inacio then Tresoldi – Milan’s plans to level up the squad outlined

The derby victory against Inter has brought a sense of excitement to AC Milan, and plans are being drawn up for a potentially busy January.

This morning’s edition of Corriere della Sera (via MilanNews) writes that Gerry Cardinale was among the happiest in attendance on Saturday night. The RedBird boss continues to reiterate his desire to bring Milan back to the top, and for this reason he’s ready to strengthen the team in January.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Not only that, but he is ready and willing to make signings that make a guaranteed difference in terms of quality, unlike last winter when the only reinforcement to arrive was Niclas Füllkrug from West Ham (now the Bundesliga top scorer).

The first move is the hiring of Markus Krosche, who will officially become the new Head of Football in the coming weeks. Milan lack someone in this role, having left it vacant since the failed summer pursuit of the German, but Cardinale didn’t give up and has got his man.

In January, the priority remains a central defender, and Gonçalo Inacio’s name remains at the top of the list. The Rossoneri are ready to try again for the Sporting CP centre-back, who – like Krösche – was pursued in the summer too.

Then there’s the mystery of Ramos’s replacement in attack, as Francesco Camarda is struggling to find playing time. So it’s possible the young striker could be sent out on loan to play consistently and continue his development.

A new centre-forward would replace him, alternating with Gonçalo Ramos. The dream would be Nicolò Tresoldi, but bringing him to Milan in the winter transfer window seems nearly impossible. The matter will likely be discussed again in the summer.
